Sports.title: Russell's theory on his big hope for F1 2027 – and Antonelli's reply
Sports.content:
From being the 2026 Formula 1 pre-season title favourite to fighting to hold on to second place as Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli accelerates into the distance, George Russell has endured a challenging few months. During that period he has been forced to question his entire approach to driving, owing to the peculiar requirements of the latest technical formula.

Most of the drivers on the grid have voiced reservations – or noisy complaints – about the unnatural driving style required to get the best out of the 2026 cars, but Russell belongs to a subset whose style appears to put them at a disadvantage compared with their team-mates. Most notably at Silverstone and Spa, Russell hit lower peak top speeds than Antonelli on key straights, explained by him using fractionally more electrical power to re-accelerate after scrubbing off more speed through preceding corners.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri is in a similar position.

Although F1's power units are shifting from a 55:45 ratio of internal combustion engine output and electrical power to 58:42 for 2027, this will not bring about a massive shift in performance characteristics. But there are other changes afoot, including a new family of Pirelli tyre compounds which have been developed through this year via testing with the current cars.

Asked in Baku ahead of this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix whether this could promote a more natural style of driving, Russell suggested that it may.

"I think it's been clear this season that the tyres, front to rear, probably have not been well balanced enough," he said. "You look at some tracks that are clearly front-limited and the fronts have stayed pretty strong throughout. It could also be because of the extra power we've got coming off the corners, so the rear tyres are getting a harder time.

"It is quite interesting. I spoke with Antonio Giovinazzi, who drove this new generation of car for the first time a couple of days ago in Imola, and he said how impressed he was at the power of these new cars off the corner. And I think that has quite an impact on the rear tyres.

"Obviously, last year when we developed these tyres, they were with the previous generation of power unit, which had much less power off the corners. So, I don't think it's a big surprise the rear tyres are getting a harder time than we all anticipated."

Action-packed 2010 Canadian Grand Prix was the catalyst for the brief handed to Pirelli when it became F1's sole tyre supplier Photo by: Getty Images

When Pirelli became F1's exclusive tyre supplier in 2011 it was handed a brief to produce compounds which offered strong grip up to a certain point in their use cycle before falling off quickly. The trigger for this was the 2010 Canadian Grand Prix. Complaints about processional racing had been building for years until this point, where a combination of a freshly resurfaced track and mixed weather in the build-up to the event caused the usually robust Bridgestone tyres to degrade rapidly, and an unpredictable race ensued.

But Pirelli has often struggled to find an ideal compromise to fulfil what is a very challenging target. The tyres have often proved too sensitive to degradation, and when Pirelli has toughened them up in response to criticism, it has overshot – not helped by being restricted in terms of how much testing it can complete with relevant machinery. Whenever testing is performed with current cars, competitive paranoia arises as teams suspect each other of covertly evaluating performance upgrades.

While the focus on developing the 2027 tyres has been on ensuring greater lap time differences between compounds, it is understood that tweaking the balance between the front and rear axle has also been on the agenda. But would better balance alone help those drivers who have been losing momentum through rear sliding, then paying the price on the straights?

That is a complicated question to answer, since these changes – even if successful – won't happen in isolation. The FIA is also bringing in a package of aerodynamic changes to curtail the downforce gains teams have been finding through developments, as well as mitigating the straight-line demand on electrical power. What the teams have discovered in simulation is that these tweaks have greater effects than first anticipated – so much so, in fact, that those who had been planning to carry over their 2026 chassis to next year for cost-control reasons have changed tack.

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

Besides tidying up some of the loopholes around the rear wing, and making it shallower, the changes mandate fewer vortex generators on the floor leading edge, as well as a significantly shorter (from 900mm to 600mm) ‘tea tray', the section of the floor that extends under the driver's legs. This latter change opens up the possibility of teams adopting very different rake angles, hence the re-think on carrying over chassis designs.

For these reasons, Antonelli takes a slightly different view from his team-mate.

"I think the tyre, also this year the tyre changed completely," he said when Autosport asked for his opinion on the magnitude of the effect the new tyres will have.

"So I think on my side, you try to understand the tyre the best way you can, and you try to adapt. I think the tyres won't be so much different, probably the front tyre will change a little bit, and in terms of structure a little bit, we'll see what Pirelli decides.

"We've done some Pirelli tests and we've given the feedback, but of course we'll see what is going to be decided. But from what we heard, it shouldn't be much different to what it was this year.

"The car will be different – on the aero side the car is changing, especially around the bib area, there's going to be a big change, which is going to implement aero loss. Then the team for sure will find a way to recover that, but the car is going to be a little bit different next year for sure.

"The baseline will be the same I think, but maybe together with the tyre and the car evolving, it's going to feel a little bit different. It's all about adapting at the end of the day, so we'll see."

There's an understandable amount of equivocation here since Antonelli didn't want to publicly contradict his team-mate. But of the Mercedes drivers he is the one who has been adapting best to the requirements of the new regulations, which he is subtly pointing out.

And of course, the risk George runs if he pins his hopes on change is that Kimi will do so again.

Sports.title: How McLaren Hypercar test will help Norris in F1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris driving McLaren’s new Hypercar may seem inconsequential in the grand scheme of Formula 1 things, but the reigning world champion would disagree.

Norris took the wheel of the MCL-HY at Algarve last week, completing just 38 laps – enough to get a feel for the World Endurance Championship’s top machinery and provide feedback to McLaren ahead of the brand’s 2027 debut.

The 26-year-old was impressed with the depth of set-up options relative to F1 and insisted it was ‘still a quick car’ when asked by Autosport about his thoughts following the test.

“The level of detail that they go into is pretty crazy,” Norris said. “They have, in some situations, a lot more scope to do things with the car than what we're allowed to do in Formula 1.

“As much as you think Formula 1 is ‘you can do whatever you want’, it's not quite that. With how you can change the toys and set up the car itself, it’s actually quite a bit more limited than you can do with the Hypercar in terms of electronics and all of these things.

“So it's pretty cool to see what you could do. It's a bit more like old-school Formula 1, when it was a bit more just a free-for-all on what you could do, which is a good thing.

“Of course, it's a very different car, it's quite a heavy car, so adapting to that; obviously quite a bit less downforce, but it still feels like a quick car, so it's still exciting.”

As a reference, Peugeot’s Malthe Jakobsen took pole position in 2m00.653s at this year’s Spa-Francorchamps 6 Hours, where F1’s 2026 benchmark was Kimi Antonelli’s 1m44.361s while Rafael Camara topped F2 qualifying in 1m56.306s.

Norris was joined at the Portuguese track by two of McLaren’s 2027 drivers, Mikkel Jensen and Laurens Vanthoor, which provided the Briton with further learning opportunities.

“It was more, again, for me to try something and also to learn things,” he said. “Everything I do, really, even when I drive other cars, is always to try and learn things – understand different styles, learn from the other drivers that I met over there, and see what I can take onboard to help me drive better this weekend.

“So it's always a good opportunity, especially to stay within the McLaren family. It helps me learn and be more focused for doing my real job, which is Formula 1.”

Norris was adamant about that last part when the 2027 Le Mans 24 Hours was brought up, given the race doesn’t clash with F1 next year – only the Test Day does.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: McLaren

“It's not something I've been thinking about, at all,” he insisted. “All my focus is still on F1, and will always be. I'll never sacrifice something in Formula 1 for something else.

“If there's a chance that things can work out, maybe, but I don't know if this is next year, the year after, three years, four years – I have no idea. Again, it's not something I've been thinking about at all, but it's something I would like to do in the future.”

Sports.title: What’s behind the delay in cancelling the Qatar and Abu Dhabi GPs?
Sports.content:
Given the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, for several months now it’s been assumed that the cancellation of the season-closing Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix is not just likely, but inevitable.

The commercial rights holder has been making contingency plans while outwardly maintaining that these races are still on. Many in the F1 paddock have followed suit: the hotels in the Imola vicinity are almost fully booked for the weekend occupied by the Abu Dhabi round.

Despite the assumption that Qatar and Abu Dhabi will inevitably be cancelled, the promoters of those races remain outwardly determined that they will go ahead as planned. Abu Dhabi has gone as far as announcing music acts including Zara Larsson, The Script, Imagine Dragons and Lewis Capaldi. Those who set store by what people say on social media will note that Larsson has subsequently claimed she will not be going.

This is all part of an ongoing dance over who would pick up the tab if those races were to be cancelled. Broadly speaking, when promoters cancel races, they are the parties who end up out of pocket since their contracts with F1 oblige them to pay the sanctioning fee anyway. If the commercial rights holder cancels the races, it forfeits those fees.

The sanctioning fees for Qatar and Abu Dhabi have been widely reported as $55million and $40million per year respectively, but it’s understood that these figures are highly speculative. Nevertheless, the sums involved are significant.

Contracts vary between promoters, especially those races which are backed by states rather than conventional commercial entities. But when events are cancelled and money is lost, there will always be a tussle over liability – especially when cancellations are enforced by outside circumstances.

Such is the commercial value of hospitality, trackside signage and other sponsorships that the potential financial fallout extends well beyond the sanctioning fees. That is why Bahrain is hosting its race in Malaysia, in effect renting the circuit so that both it and F1 can fulfil their contractual obligations.

F1 is going to Malaysia for the Bahrain GP this year Photo by: Peter J Fox / Getty Images

“We will take the decision at the right time,” said F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali at the end of July. “That moment will be not before the middle of September. For us today, the races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are confirmed.



“By the way, they are already sold out. That is an incredible sign of how much the sport is bigger than the problem that our world is living. But of course, if the situation would not be clearer the way that we believe it should be, before the middle of September, we will take the decision.”

Besides showing a rather tone-deaf perspective on F1’s importance in relation to geopolitics, this pronouncement also muddied the picture of when the decision would be made: before or after the middle of September? Either way, this date has now passed.

Domenicali also confirmed that if the final two rounds were cancelled, the season would not end with a double-header in Las Vegas. Despite some sources still claiming such an event is likely, it is not. F1 already has to tread carefully around the other Las Vegas stakeholders and it is understood that holding back-to-back events there would definitely not be welcomed by the local business community. A double-header would also clash with the Thanksgiving holiday.

The requirement to find a home for a final round in the event of the Qatar and Abu Dhabi GPs not happening is also contractual. As it stands, if they were to disappear from the calendar, F1 would be left with 21 rounds. While this would enable it to fulfil the majority of its broadcast contracts, it’s understood that at least one stipulates 22.

Imola was viewed as a shoo-in for the season finale but, during the Italian Grand Prix weekend, it emerged that F1 has experienced significant pushback from Qatar and Abu Dhabi regarding the cancellation of their rounds. It is understood their position is one of business as usual, since they have not been targeted by Iran for several months.

Imola had been cued up to host an impromptu F1 finale Photo by: Steven Tee / Motorsport Images

Difficult days therefore lie ahead for the commercial rights holder, since it will be required to make a decision soon for logistical reasons. In its quest to reach net zero emissions by 2030, F1 now transports a great deal of equipment via sea. This naturally means longer lead times.

Beyond the timescales involved in sea-freighting infrastructure to the Gulf region, there is the practical question of it having to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint which opens and closes depending on the state of hostilities between Iran and the USA. Should the final rounds remain as presently scheduled, more freight would have to go by air, increasing costs as well as emissions.

And while this game of brinksmanship evolves between the commercial rights holder and the Middle Eastern promoters, the teams also have questions to ask. Should their respective governments' foreign offices advise against travel to the Middle East, they will not be insured.

But at the moment, the British government's advice is: "All British nationals currently in the Middle East should be prepared for possible flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions." The US Department of State says putative visitors to the region should "reconsider". Neither of these amounts to a warning not to travel.

As such, it's understood that the risk of cancellation for these final two rounds is receding.

Sports.title: "Free agent" Ocon talking to other teams with Haas yet to confirm F1 2027 line-up
Sports.content:
Esteban Ocon declared himself a "free agent" as Haas is yet to confirm its driver line-up for the 2027 Formula 1 season, but did not rule out potentially staying at the team.

Although the Frenchman has been enjoying much improved performances of late, which have gone largely unrewarded as Haas' performance has slipped away from its early-season points-scoring form, Ocon's seat has been under threat for some time.

Haas has been using its testing of previous cars (TPC) programme to identify a potential partner for Oliver Bearman next season, with Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, reigning F2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli, and current reserve Ryo Hirakawa in the frame.

Ocon confirmed that he was looking for other options for 2027, while Haas continues to assess its driver pairing for next year.

Recent rumours have surfaced suggesting that the team is leaning towards Camara - currently the reigning F3 champion and second in this year's F2 standings - although team boss Ayao Komatsu stated during the Spanish GP that he had "maybe five" drivers in contention.

"Yes, at the moment I am definitely a free agent for next year," Ocon stated. "There are things in discussion that are out of my control and there are certain topics that are out of my control. So I will keep pushing until the end of the year and see how it goes."

Asked if staying at Haas was an option, Ocon remained tight-lipped and responded: "Let's see."

Esteban Ocon, Haas Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Ocon added that he was pleased with his performances of late, having suffered this season with an inconsistent car in the early stages of the season.

It is unclear if this is an aerodynamic sensitivity issue or a parts quality control problem; Komatsu has suggested both could be causes, and that the team is still investigating the issue at hand.

"We know it's been an ongoing issue," he said. "It's reassuring that I'm doing a good job. Obviously, my performance hasn't been an issue this year.

"I've performed every time I had the car. I've been the last one to score in Monaco. I was almost scoring in Madrid. There's been a lot of times where I've performed when the car was underperforming. It's been clear.

"Everybody in the team has been following that very closely, trying to fix the problem. We haven't been hiding from it. But it's been quite disappointing at times, obviously, to have these kind of problems."

Bearman was asked if he felt ready to step up as the team leader should Ocon depart, and the Briton stated that he'd learned a lot from his team-mate across the almost two years spent together as team-mates.

Esteban Ocon, Haas F1 Team, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

He pointed to Ocon's feedback in the engineering room as something that he'd taken inspiration from, along with his own improving performances on-track.

"I've been here for, well, this is my second year driving as a full-time driver, but also I've been one year as a reserve for Haas, also did a few races and FP1s the year before that, even in 2023, I did my first FP1. So I have a really good level of experience with the team," Bearman said.

"I feel like I've improved a lot in terms of my on-track performance, but also how I describe what I'm feeling in the car and things like that. And that's something I certainly learned a lot from someone who's very experienced like Esteban. So on that side, it's been really good learning for me.

"Even if I compare my feedback to 12 months ago, I'm not sure I would have the confidence to just rely on my own feedback. But I feel like I've made a good step in that regard, and it's just a normal learning process, really."

Sports.title: The initial plan for F1's next engine regulation in 2030
Sports.content:
Formula 1 stakeholders have reached an agreement on the main elements of the next engine rules cycle.

The FIA and F1 engine manufacturers have opted against a naturally aspirated option, partly because of noise restrictions at street circuits, with a smaller and simplified electronics package.

A push-to-pass overtake mode is also under consideration, along with a possible debut in 2030.

While discussions are still ongoing, the engine set to define the next technical cycle in F1 has largely taken shape. Meetings between the FIA and the manufacturers will continue to finalise the remaining details, but a substantial agreement has been reached on the key points with the focus on a simpler and lighter power unit, one that is considered closer to the traditional concept of a racing engine.

A return to V8 engines

F1 is set to move to 3.0-litre V8 architecture, but one of the issues that most divided the engine manufacturers was whether to retain the turbocharger.

The possibility of opting for a naturally aspirated engine was also on the table, a solution that would have delivered a sound particularly appealing to fans nostalgic for F1 in the early 2000s.

Fernando Alonso, Renault R25, leads Michael Schumacher, Ferrari F2005 Photo by: Motorsport Images

However, the turbocharger element will remain as part of the power unit configuration, but the reasons behind the decision go beyond purely technical considerations.

A naturally aspirated 3.0-litre V8 would have reached noise levels that would cause a major problem with some of the current F1 venues.

The issue concerns street circuits in particular: Melbourne, Miami, Madrid, Singapore, Baku and Las Vegas are venues where noise-emission restrictions are in place, and the arrival of cars significantly louder than the current generation could create major difficulties that would be impossible to overcome and potentially even put some events at risk.

This has led to the decision to retain a smaller turbocharger, a compromise that should still make it possible to achieve a considerably louder sound than that of the current power units, while keeping noise levels within limits applied at some F1 circuits.

Smaller electrical motor and lighter power units

The new V8 will not be completely detached from electrification either. The new rules look set to include a simplified 100kW electric motor, a considerably lower output than the 350kW current generation of power units.

The aim is to maintain a technological link with the automotive industry without replicating the complexity that has characterised the latest generation of power units. The direction emerging from the discussions is clear: electric power will remain part of F1, but with a less dominant role within the overall package.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

Another area where the lessons of recent years appear to have been taken on board concern the weight of the overall power unit. The target set for the new power unit is highly ambitious: to produce a complete unit weighing at least 50kg lighter than the current power units.

Push-to-pass and 2030 introduction being considered

Some aspects still need to be finalised. Among them is the system that will give drivers an additional power boost to assist overtaking manoeuvres.

There appears to be no intention to bring back the DRS used until the end of the 2025 season. The solution currently under consideration is closer to the push-to-pass philosophy adopted in IndyCar: a temporary increase in power that the driver could deploy under specific circumstances.

This will be one of the areas the FIA and the engine manufacturers still need to reach a definitive agreement on.

When the new regulations will be introduced in F1 also remains open, with the plan to debut the new rules in 2030 an option, which would bring forward the end of the current technical rules cycle that began by one year.

Reaching a decision will require all parties to find common ground, but the issues that have emerged with the current generation of power units have accelerated a broader discussion that goes beyond individual technical details. After pushing hard on technological complexity, F1 appears keen to return to a more traditional concept of a racing engine.

Sports.title: Russell fastest as hydraulic problem halts Antonelli in first practice | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell led the opening practice session for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix while a technical problem delayed his team mate.

Russell’s best lap, aided by a significant slipstream from a rival car, was exactly four-tenths of a second quicker than the next-closest driver, Max Verstappen. However Russell’s session almost came to an early end when he abandoned his attempt to take turn three and swerved into the run-off area, narrowly missing the barrier as he did.

Verstappen began the session strongly. The Red Bull driver was fastest over the opening 10 minutes, running on hard tyres, before Antonelli beat his time.

Despite his stoppage, the world championship leader ended the session with the fifth-fastest time. The two Ferrari drivers also beat him, Charles Leclerc only fractionally slower than Verstappen.

Liam Lawson returned to Racing Bulls after his brief stint at Red Bull’s senior team and set the sixth-fastest time. Isack Hadjar, back in the car Lawson drove in the last three races, was only able to do eight laps before Red Bull told him to stop due to a technical problem.

Nico Hulkenberg put his heavily updated Audi seventh-fastest. He briefly came to a stop near the end of the session but was able to resume.

Oscar Piastri set the eighth-fastest time with his final lap of the session. His running in McLaren’s updated MCL40 was disrupted when the team identified a potential problem on his team mate’s car and told him to stop, though Piastri was able to rejoin the track for a final lap.

Sports.title: Social Media: Ben Sulayem defends Gasly after latest abuse from Colapinto fans | Brief
Sports.content:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has condemned the online abuse directed at Pierre Gasly by supporters of his team mate.

Gasly briefly delayed Franco Colapinto during the latter stages of the Spanish Grand Prix two weeks ago. The driver and his family have since received abusive messages on social media.

“The online abuse directed at Pierre Gasly and his family is completely unacceptable,” said Ben Sulayem in a post. “Pierre has my full support, and I strongly condemn this behaviour. No driver, official, volunteer or fan should have to face this.

“Incidents like this are why I founded the United Against Online Abuse initiative. We simply cannot accept online hate within our sport and we all have a responsibility – governing bodies, teams, drivers, fans and social media platforms – to challenge this behaviour and create an environment built on respect.”

Colapinto’s supporters have been repeatedly accused of aiming abuse at drivers and other figures in the sport, including Jack Doohan last year, his own team this year and the FIA’s stewards last month.

“Competition and passion are at the heart of motorsport, but abuse has no place in it,” Ben Sulayem added. “We must continue to stand together and take meaningful action to protect everyone in our sporting community.”

Sports.title: Ocon confirms he is a “free agent” for 2027 as rumours link Camara to Haas | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Esteban Ocon looks set to leave Haas at the end of the season as the driver admitted he is a “free agent” for 2027.

The 30-year-old joined the team from Alpine last year. He was out-scored by rookie team mate Oliver Bearman last year and lies behind his team mate in the standings.

“At the moment I’m definitely a free agent for next year,” said Ocon in Baku. “[There are] all these discussions and there are certain topics in the background that are out of my control at this moment. So I’m focused on the track, trying to deliver the best I can and getting the result that this team deserves.”

Neither Haas driver has scored since Ocon’s ninth-place finish in Monaco.

Ocon said he’s been “really happy with my personal performance” lately. “I think I’ve been getting the maximum out of the car for quite a while now and we’ve never doubted about it.

“Of course, when the car is working, it helps [you] to get something better. When the inconsistencies of the cars are here, where you struggle more, you don’t look as good.

“But I know that I’m exploiting the maximum of the package that I have every single time. So that’s strong.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Ocon ran 10th at the last round in Madrid prior to his pit stop, but fell to 11th at the finish.

“I’m the last one to have scored for the team in Monaco, but it’s been a while. But we were [running] in the points in Madrid, we got both Audis at the start, and we lost it in the pit lane. So this is something we will get stronger on now. But it was a very strong weekend.

“I’m happy with my performance. So we need to keep going here, hopefully have another strong one. There’s usually things happening on this track so I’m looking forward to driving here.”

Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara, who is currently second in the Formula 2 standings, has been linked to the team. Bearman is also part of Ferrari’s young driver programme.

Sports.title: Antonelli has “perfect driving style” for 2026 cars – Russell | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is enjoying an extraordinarily successful second season in Formula 1 because his driving style works perfectly with the current generation of cars, says his team mate.

George Russell is Antonelli’s closest rival at the top of the championship standings, but the second-year driver is 81 points ahead. This is a sharp contrast to last year, when Russell out-scored Antonelli by 319 points to 150.

While Russell said Antonelli’s ability was clear before this season, he believes the reduction in aerodynamic downforce and grip this year has played to his team mate’s strengths.

“Of course Kimi is extremely talented,” said Russell. “He’s an incredible driver and has been fast in his whole career.

“I think his driving style is very similar to what he had last year and I think with just how things have fallen this year, it’s kind of the perfect driving style for these cars.”

Russell believes the same is true of other drivers, including Lando Norris, who is the only driver to have won more than one round this season.

“If you look last year, there are definitely trends,” said Russell. “If you look at Brazil last year, Kimi had a really strong race and Lando won in Brazil, and they’re two drivers who are always very strong on the low grip tracks and they’re two drivers who are arguably the best-performing drivers of this season.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“He’s an amazing driver and he was of course doing extremely well last year as well. Let’s see next year if it changes or not, but certainly his natural driving style suits very well for this regulation.”

Charles Leclerc echoed Russell’s view that Antonelli’s potential was clear despite his patchy rookie campaign last year.

“I wish I knew, but clearly he’s doing something that works very well,” said Leclerc. “But to be honest, it’s not that it comes as a complete surprise.

“If I look at Kimi going through the junior ranks, I think it was quite clear for everybody that he had something very special. If you look obviously at his first year in Formula 1, I think he probably faced challenges – it is not up to me to go into detail, I don’t know, but surely he had some struggles in the first year – but this year has been extremely impressive. I mean, from the first race to now, he’s been perfect and driving at a very high level against a driver that I rate extremely high as well, which is George. So he’s doing an incredible job.”

However Leclerc said there is only so much he can tell about Antonelli’s qualities from outside the Mercedes team.

“To [tell] you exactly why he’s so fast, and why he is outstandingly fast this year compared to last year, is very difficult for me. We are all here analysing the data of everybody but we can only go up to a certain amount of detail, then you really need the data of the actual car to dig into more detail.

“So it’s difficult. But his laps look a lot on the limit but somehow he manages to do the lap when it counts and that’s been very impressive to watch.”

Sports.title: Hadjar says injured wrist is “still going to be painful for a while” after comeback | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar says he is still in pain from his injured wrist as he returns to racing this weekend.

The Red Bull driver, who has missed the last three rounds, said his wrist is “good enough to drive, so that’s all I need.”

He said no surgery was required on the injury and a pre-event simulator session indicated it is now strong enough for him to be able to drive.

“I have a small fracture on the outside of the wrist and it’s just quite a long process,” said Hadjar. “I didn’t need any surgery so it’s all natural and it takes some time.

“It’s still going to be painful for a while. It’s going to be six weeks.

“It says that it’s strong enough at the moment to resist the tensions. I had a test on the sim, it went well. I think it’s a similar environment as the cockpit. It’s actually, if anything, nearly identical. So if it’s fine on the sim, with the adrenaline on track and everything, I think I should be okay.

“It’s just been the training sessions have not been fun because I’ve been doing basically nothing with the left limb, so it’s been a bit boring.”

Hadjar confirmed he spoke to multiple Moto GP champion Marc Marquez, who has broken many bones during his career, notably in 2020 when he made an early return from one injury only to sustain another. Hadjar said Marquez told him: “Not to race.”

Red Bull confirmed today Hadjar will continue to drive for them next season. Hadjar said the news is “good, it is nice, but it is natural.”

“I’m not here to be hopeful,” he explained. “I’m here to show what I do on track and naturally, the rest comes, so it’s normal in a way.”

Sports.title: Excessive focus on battle between Ferrari drivers is “not fair” – Leclerc | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc says too much attention has been paid to the on-track battle between him and his team mate, particularly since their clash at Monza.

The Ferrari driver has already admitted he went too far in his first-lap battle with Lewis Hamilton when he forced his team mate wide at turn two.

“Turn two in Monza is something that I’ve said repeatedly is not something that we want to see ever happen again,” said Leclerc. “And that [was] going too far on my side.

“But I’ve been through it already. I think it’s pretty clear that we don’t necessarily have to write [rules of engagement for] those things, I think it’s clear enough.

“But again, I feel like it’s being over-discussed and over-analysed when it’s about the red cars, and that’s not really fair.”

He alluded to incidents between the McLaren and Mercedes drivers during the final laps of the same race. “In Monza, if you look at the four top teams, three of them had fights like this with a car finishing in the grass, and at the end of the day, the only thing we are speaking about still now is the red car, which I don’t think is fair.”

Leclerc said both drivers have exceeded the limits of what is acceptable at times but he is happy with how they race wheel-to-wheel.

“Of course there’s been moments where I went too far, where Lewis went too far, but I think the key in that is to discuss,” he said. “I’ve been with Ferrari since 2019 now and I know how everything we do is over-analysed, over-discussed and very often the conclusions that are taken after those kind of fights are the wrong ones.

Sports.title: “Money fears” delay F1’s decision on whether Middle East races will happen – report | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula One Management is delaying its decision over whether to cancel the final two rounds of the season due to concerns over money, according to a report in The Times.

F1 will not receive its huge fees from the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grand prix promoters if it calls off the races. If the promoters make the decision to cancel, they will bear the costs.

But the longer F1 leaves the decision, the harder it may be to organise a replacement for either race. Cancelling a race would reduce the number of points available and could affect the championship situation, potentially even deciding it. Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads the championship by 81 points with 233 available.

Domenicali has indicated F1 has a plan to replace the Abu Dhabi finale if that cannot go ahead. This is believed to be a race at Imola in Italy.

F1 has already cancelled the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian grands prix as a result of the war. A replacement for the former, titled the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, will take place next week at the Sepang International Circuit.

Earlier this month FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said the governing body will be guided by local promoters on whether the events could go ahead.

“Being from that part of the world, we can’t jump the gun and just say, that’s it, we are cancelling and then cancel,” he said.

“Are we going to allow our people, our staff, the drivers or the teams to go at risk? No, of course not. We will not. But we’ll have to also listen to the governments and to the local promoter there.”

Sports.title: Red Bull confirms Hadjar will remain as Verstappen’s team mate in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull has given a vote of confidence to Isack Hadjar, extending his contract to drive for the team again next year.

Hadjar made his debut in Formula 1 last year with Red Bull’s second team, Racing Bulls, before being promoted to their leading squad this year.

“Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track,” said team principal Laurent Mekies, “especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision.”

Although Hadjar did not compete in the last three rounds due to injury, Hadjar made an impressive start to life at Red Bull, taking a podium finish in his sixth appearance in Monaco. Before being forced out due to injury he had scored 71 points to Verstappen’s 109.

Red Bull has struggled to find an effective team mate to pair Verstappen with. The team handed Sergio Perez a two-year contract extension during 2024 but dropped him at the end of the year for Liam Lawson. Perez’s replacement lasted just two rounds at the start of last year before Red Bull dropped him. Yuki Tsunoda, who replaced Lawson, ended the season with the largest points deficit to a team mate ever seen in F1, leading Red Bull to make another change.

Mekies said Hadjar performed well from the outset after moving up to Red Bull. He will race for the team this weekend in Baku for the first time since the Hungarian Grand Prix in July.

“You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat,” said Mekies. “The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can’t wait to see him back out on track.”

Hadjar said he is “really excited” by his new deal. “From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I’ve been able to justify the faith they’ve had in me,” he said. “I’m constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs  Anthony Joshua Finally Official: December 11 in Cardiff on Netflix
Sports.content:
The British heavyweight rivals will meet at Principality Stadium after a dispute over the venue delayed their long-awaited fight.

Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) and Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) will finally fight on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, live on Netflix. The confirmation ends months of negotiations over where the British heavyweight clash would take place.

The venue dispute is settled. Joshua’s camp had insisted on staging the bout in Britain, while New York’s Madison Square Garden became a serious alternative.

“I can now confirm that Fury Vs Joshua will be coming to the UK, as I promised British boxing fans. The time for talking is over……..” Turki Alalshikh wrote on X.

Both fighters signed earlier this year. A date and venue remained unresolved, however, allowing the dispute to drag on despite their agreement to face each other. Fury repeatedly blamed Joshua in public and suggested he could pursue a third fight against Oleksandr Usyk.

Dana White said: “For more than a decade, boxing fans have been clamoring for the heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Together, they bring 66 wins, 52 knockouts and multiple heavyweight world titles into the ring. On December 11, two of the biggest heavyweights of this generation finally collide and the winner will take a significant place in heavyweight history.”

Joshua has boxed at Principality Stadium twice before, stopping Carlos Takam and then outpointing Joseph Parker to add the WBO heavyweight belt to his collection. He returns to face the British rival whose name has followed him through years of callouts and failed negotiations.

Both men came through summer bouts.

Joshua survived two first-round knockdowns against Kristian Prenga in July before stopping him in the second. Fury stopped Mariusz Wach after seven rounds in Thailand that month, having returned in April to outpoint Aslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Those victories kept their meeting alive. Now the former heavyweight champions have a confirmed December date in Britain, with Netflix carrying the broadcast.

Sports.title: Manny Pacquiao and Shakur Stevenson Remain in Cardiff Talks
Sports.content:
Manny Pacquiao against Shakur Stevenson remains under discussion for the proposed Anthony Joshua-Tyson Fury card in Cardiff. It would give the event a second major fight, but neither Pacquiao nor Stevenson has received a bout agreement.

BoxingScene’s Lance Pugmire reports that two people connected to the talks say Netflix wants the matchup as part of a “double main event.” December 11 is the date under consideration at Principality Stadium, with December 18 also possible. Pacquiao adviser Jas Mathur told BoxingScene that Pacquiao’s financial terms are still being negotiated.

That leaves a great deal to settle before anyone can call this a fight. The Cardiff show itself has yet to be formally announced, and moving Joshua-Fury from the previously discussed Madison Square Garden setting means assembling the rest of the card around a different venue and date.

Pacquiao-Stevenson would bring two very different attractions to that card. Stevenson, 29, is coming off his January win over Teofimo Lopez and has since signed with Zuffa Boxing. Pacquiao, 47, drew with Mario Barrios in his July 2025 return. His name would draw attention far beyond the usual boxing audience, though the long layoff and age difference would become part of the conversation as soon as the fight was announced.

The proposed pairing also raises a practical question: what weight would they fight at? Pacquiao’s return came at welterweight, while Stevenson’s recent work has been at lighter weights. No weight, number of rounds, or title terms have been announced.

For now, the news is that Pacquiao-Stevenson has survived the reported switch to Cardiff and remains in Netflix’s plans, according to BoxingScene. The decisive development would be agreements reaching both fighters. Until then, it belongs on the list of fights being negotiated, rather than the Joshua-Fury undercard.

Pacquiao turns 48 on December 17. If the fight lands on December 18, Shakur would face him one day after his birthday. Pacquiao won his first world title in 1998, before Shakur turned two.

That age difference makes the matchup a hard sell as a competitive fight. If Shakur wins easily, how much credit does he get for beating a man nearly two decades older? If he boxes his way to a quiet decision, Pacquiao’s name may bring viewers to Netflix, but the fight may give them little reason to watch Shakur again.

Pacquiao’s fame can make this a major event. Turning it into a fight that helps Shakur is another matter. First, both men need to agree to terms; neither has received a bout agreement.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Picks Leonard, But Ray Robinson Set The Harder Standard
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson prefers Sugar Ray Leonard to Sugar Ray Robinson. It is easy to see why. Leonard’s speed, movement, and command of distance resemble the qualities Shakur prizes in his own boxing. But Leonard’s finest wins also required him to fight through danger, and Robinson did that across a schedule neither man came close to matching.

“I like SRL better then I like SRR, This might make my people mad but SRL was one hellavu fighter to me his level was extremely high!!” said Shakur on X.

Stevenson posted that on X on September 22. He had previously called Robinson “buns,” then conceded Robinson was a great fighter and said he had been talking trash. His preference for Leonard is consistent with that view.

Leonard was no fighter who simply ran from trouble. He lost a hard 15 rounds to Roberto Durán, came back to beat him, and stopped Thomas Hearns late in their first fight. His footwork gave him choices; when those fights demanded more, he had offense and resolve to draw upon.

Robinson’s record makes the comparison tougher for Shakur. At age 29, Robinson was 108-1-2 with 72 knockouts. Shakur Stevenson (25-0, 11 KOs) has fought 25 times at the same age. Leonard had fought 34. Different eras produced different schedules, but Robinson’s total still speaks to his ability to win, recover, and do it again.

Shakur’s defense is exceptional. What remains unproven is how he would respond if his legs slowed and an opponent forced him to fight for long stretches at close range. Leonard showed he had answers when movement was insufficient. Robinson showed them more than a hundred times before his 29th birthday, backed by power Shakur has yet to display.

Shakur can like Leonard better. If he is judging the full range of what a fighter had to survive and deliver, Robinson deserves a closer look.

Nobody from modern eras, Leonard included, touches what Robinson accomplished by 29.

Robinson was 128-1-2 with 84 knockouts by the time he hit his 30th birthday, and that lone defeat to Jake LaMotta was avenged multiple times over. He was fighting every few weeks, traveling by car or train, taking on rugged contenders in 15-round fights with small gloves and no modern sports science. If Leonard had tried to keep that exact pace against that level of weekly attrition, his body would have broken down even sooner. Leonard had brittle hands and a detached retina by fight 28. Robinson had a jaw made of granite, brutal endurance, and lethal power in both hands.

Shakur picking Leonard makes sense purely through the lens of modern comfort. Leonard represents the blueprint Shakur relates to: the flashy television superstar, the Olympic gold medalist, the master of lateral movement, hand speed, and distance management. Leonard showed that a fighter could dictate terms, generate huge paydays, and maintain an aura without having to fight forty times a year in smoke-filled arenas.

Where Shakur’s comparison falls completely flat is what Leonard actually did when boxing finesse failed. When Leonard got pulled into absolute hell against Roberto Duran in Montreal, he stood flat-footed and fought. When he was fading and behind on the cards against Thomas Hearns, he unleashed a vicious, predatory assault to close the show. Leonard had a ruthless finishing instinct.

Shakur takes the defensive, perimeter-oriented parts of Leonard’s style and strips away the violent bite. Robinson was a destructive puncher who could knock an opponent out going backward or forward. Shakur is a pure points collector who treats contact like a disaster.

Shakur looking at Robinson and favoring Leonard sounds like modern revisionism. It is a fighter who relies on safety and low output, trying to validate his own approach, overlooking the fact that both Sugar Rays had an appetite for destruction that Shakur has never shown inside a ring.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia May Vacate Rather Than Fight Bektemir Melikuziev
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia may give up his WBA super middleweight title rather than defend it against Bektemir Melikuziev. Rick Glaser says Munguia’s team is considering that option. If his information is right, the decision would fit a career that has generally been managed with care. I expected Munguia’s team to have little appetite for Bek once the mandatory fight was ordered.

Glaser says Munguia’s camp is taking a “deep dive into the idea of giving up the title.” He has not said Munguia has vacated. The WBA has given the two sides until October 21 to make a deal and may call a purse bid if they fail to agree.

The Golden Boy connection makes this especially revealing. Melikuziev has fought under its banner since turning professional, and the company knows what its own fighter would bring against Munguia. Bek is a powerful southpaw with a damaging body attack. Munguia’s willingness to take punches while pressing forward would give him chances to land, but it would also give Bek chances to hurt him.

Munguia (46-2, 35 KOs) accepted the Canelo Alvarez fight for a huge payday and lost. Bruno Surace then knocked him out in a matchup Munguia was favored to win. Sergiy Derevyanchenko gave Munguia a hard fight, so his record is not free of risk. Melikuziev presents a different calculation: considerable danger with nowhere near Canelo’s commercial reward.

The WBA belt helped Munguia regain world champion status when he beat José Armando Reséndiz in May. Defending it is another matter. A purse bid could also take the choice of date, venue, and broadcaster out of his team’s hands. Vacating would leave Munguia free to pursue a bigger name at 168, though that freedom would come at Bek’s expense.

Melikuziev (17-1, 11 KOs) beat Darius Fulghum in a WBA eliminator in May 2025, then watched Munguia get the fight with Reséndiz. Bek told The Ring he had been assured he would get the next shot. If Munguia vacates, Bek may still get a chance to win the belt. He would lose the chance to win it from Munguia, a victory that would mean far more for his career.

We’re seeing the new age of belt-holders. Champions giving up their belts exposes the entire modern hustle around world titles. Fighters treat sanctioning body belts like disposable leverage tools rather than something to defend against legitimate threats. They want the belt purely to slap “world champion” on a poster, collect the promotional bump, and leverage it into an in-house payday.

The second a dangerous, low-profile puncher gets ordered as a mandatory, they drop the trinket in the trash and run. Look at the pattern playing out right now. Hamzah Sheeraz walked away from his belt rather than get in the ring with Janibek Alimkhanuly. Teofimo Lopez is on the verge of playing the same game,

Now Jaime Munguia’s camp looks ready to dump the WBA strap because Bektemir Melikuziev offers pure risk with zero casual crossover appeal. Bektemir is a nightmare matchup for a flawed fighter like Munguia. Bek is a heavy-handed, compact southpaw who specializes in cracking the ribs and punishing guys who march forward without defense.

Against Bektemir, Munguia risks getting stopped on regular DAZN for modest money, completely torpedoing his marketability for another mega-fight. Dumping the title completely strips away the pretense of championship prestige. Decades ago, winning a belt meant you took on whoever climbed the ladder, regardless of style or reward. What we’re seeing now is champions treating mandatory defenses like bad business propositions.

If Munguia vacates, Bektemir Melikuziev should get the first chance at the vacant WBA title, but the WBA would still have to choose his opponent. Its current rankings put Canelo Alvarez at No. 2 and José Armando Reséndiz at No. 3. A Canelo fight would be the biggest prize for Bek, though there is no indication Canelo wants it.

Reséndiz looks like the more realistic choice: he lost the belt to Munguia in May and would have a chance to win it back. That would give Bek a title opportunity, but it would deny him the higher-profile victory over Munguia that he has spent more than a year pursuing.

Sports.title: Cuban Boxing Greatness Crossed a Dividing Line
Sports.content:
Cuba produced professional stars before it became an Olympic boxing power. That history makes any list of its greatest fighters difficult to rank. Kid Chocolate and Kid Gavilan built their names in long professional careers; Teófilo Stevenson and Félix Savón never fought professionally. The dividing line was a political decision in 1962 that changed what a Cuban boxer could do with his talent.

Chocolate was a major New York attraction in the 1930s, admired for his speed and two-handed punching. Gavilan later won the welterweight title and made the bolo punch his signature. Luis Rodriguez added another championship to Cuba’s professional history when he beat Emile Griffith for the welterweight title in 1963. These men built their reputations in fights against the leading professionals of their day.

After Cuba banned professional boxing, a fighter who wanted that career had to pursue it abroad. José Nápoles became a welterweight champion after making his home in Mexico. José Legrá won the featherweight title while based in Spain. Later fighters such as Erislandy Lara left Cuba to compete for professional titles. Their success carried a personal cost that a list of wins and belts cannot show.

Cuba also built an amateur program under coach Alcides Sagarra that produced generations of Olympic champions. Stevenson won heavyweight gold in 1972, 1976 and 1980. Savón won the same prize in 1992, 1996 and 2000. Their medals need no imagined professional careers to give them value. But the absence of professional fights leaves one question open: how would the system’s best have performed against established champions over twelve rounds?

Guillermo Rigondeaux gave that question a partial answer. He won Olympic gold in 2000 and 2004, then left Cuba and became a professional champion. In 2013, he beat Nonito Donaire in a super bantamweight title fight, controlling distance and making a dangerous puncher miss repeatedly. Donaire was a proven champion, and Rigondeaux’s amateur schooling held up against him. One fight cannot settle how Stevenson or Savón would have fared as professionals, but it gives this comparison something firmer than speculation.

Lara’s December 2025 defense of the WBA middleweight title shows that Cuban fighters still succeed on the professional side of that divide. The strongest case for Cuba’s boxing greatness comes from looking at both sides: champions who proved themselves over long professional careers, Olympic greats whose careers took another course, and Rigondeaux, who crossed between them and beat one of the best.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Faces Conor Wallace With Little Buzz
Sports.content:
Matchroom’s countdown poster for the October 3 fight puts Ben Whittaker front and center in gold gloves, treating Conor Wallace like an afterthought tucked near the bottom. That tells you everything about how this IBF final eliminator is being sold. Matchroom wants the spectacle, yet they are hiding the very man brought in to provide a test at Birmingham’s Utilita Arena on DAZN.

The sanctioning body slapped a number two ranking on Wallace, dangling a mandatory shot at Dmitry Bivol for the victor. Matchroom calls this Whittaker’s most demanding fight to date, yet their own promotional material treats Wallace like a ghost.

Wallace is a heavy-handed southpaw who thrives on forward pressure, precisely the style that gave Whittaker fits against Liam Cameron. Cameron refused to play along with the showboating, got right in Whittaker’s chest, took away his operating room, and forced a difficult inside brawl that ended in a bizarre technical draw. That fight exposed the cracks in Whittaker’s viral persona.

Whittaker loves dropping his hands, leaning back, and relying on pure reflexes against timid opposition. A southpaw stepping outside the lead foot and drilling straight left hands down the pipe shatters that rhythm instantly. If Wallace gets past the jab, cuts off the ring, and forces Whittaker into the ropes, the fancy footwork disappears, leaving a grueling night of trench warfare.

Wallace built that top ranking touring the regional Australian circuit, highlighted by a narrow split decision win over Jerome Pampellone. Whittaker, despite his Olympic silver medal pedigree, spent his recent dates clowning against Richard Rivera, Braian Nahuel Suarez, and Benjamin Gavazi. Both fighters avoided the domestic shark tank of Joshua Buatsi, Willy Hutchinson, or Anthony Yarde to land in this position.

Taking an open sanctioning door is standard boxing business, but Dmitry Bivol waits on the other side. Bivol dismantles loose showmen with relentless robotic fundamentals, punishing anyone who drops their hands. Wallace is the final chance to discover if Whittaker has actual substance when an opponent fires back with bad intentions, and Matchroom is foolish to hide the danger.

Eddie Hearn labels Ben Whittaker a generational talent, but Matchroom matches him like an unpolished novice they are terrified of getting touched. If a promoter genuinely believes an Olympic silver medalist is that caliber of fighter, you do not keep him in bubble wrap for four years. Look at genuine generational fighters or top-tier Olympians: Vasiliy Lomachenko was fighting for a world title in his second professional bout. Sugar Ray Leonard, Floyd Mayweather Jr., and Andre Ward were dismantling legitimate, battle-tested contenders by their thirteenth fight.

Whittaker is 29 years old. He is not a 20-year-old kid who needs physical maturation or time to grow into his man strength. At his age, an elite fighter should be in his prime, yet Matchroom is treating this October 3 date with Conor Wallace like a massive hurdle rather than what it actually is: an exercise in matchmaking self-preservation.

Wallace is an eight-year pro whose record looks manufactured in a lab. He racked up wins on the Australian circuit against obscure opposition, barely edged Jerome Pampellone by split decision, and somehow landed the IBF number two ranking because the sanctioning bodies operate on regional belt accumulation rather than quality. S

erious boxing fans know Wallace is not a top ten light heavyweight in the world. He is a convenient mark with an inflated ranking.The fact that Matchroom selected Wallace for an IBF final eliminator instead of testing Whittaker against domestic threats tells the whole story. Why hasn’t Whittaker been matched against Joshua Buatsi, Anthony Yarde, Willy Hutchinson, or Dan Azeez? Those are the domestic names that would force Whittaker to prove he belongs.

Matchroom deliberately avoided that gauntlet because they know what happens when someone refuses to buy into the showmanship. The Liam Cameron fight gave away the game. When Cameron got inside, roughed Whittaker up, and took away his operating space, the flashy reflex defense fell apart. Whittaker looked ordinary, rattled, and completely out of ideas before that bizarre ring fall ended things in a technical draw. That reveals what Hearn and his team likely see behind closed doors in sparring. If a fighter looks unbeatable in the gym against world-class work, a promoter moves him fast to cash in.

When a promoter slow walks a 29-year-old Olympic medalist against handpicked opposition, it means the gym reports are raising red flags: leaks in the defensive fundamentals, getting clipped when trading on the inside, or an engine that cannot handle a relentless twelve-round pace.

It appears that Matchroom is trying to sneak Whittaker through an open back door to a massive payday against Dmitry Bivol without having him run a real gauntlet. Wallace was brought in to provide the illusion of a world-level eliminator without the actual danger. If Whittaker were the transcendent force Hearn claims, the training wheels would have come off years ago.

Sports.title: Gerrie Coetzee’s Bionic Hand Ends Michael Dokes’s Reign
Sports.content:
Michael Dokes had the faster hands and a title defense close to home on September 23, 1983. Gerrie Coetzee had two failed title bids and a reputation for fading late. Ten rounds later, Dokes was on the canvas, and Coetzee was the WBA heavyweight champion.

Don King billed the fight at Richfield Coliseum as “The Buckeye Homecoming,” though the crowd was about 7,000 in an arena that held 22,000. Dokes (26-0-2, 15 KOs), from nearby Akron, was a 5-1 favorite over Coetzee (28-3-1, 17 KOs). His title reign had begun with a disputed first-round stoppage of Mike Weaver, followed by a draw in their rematch.

Coetzee knew how a strong start could go wrong. John Tate had outlasted him over 15 rounds, and Weaver had stopped him in the 13th. Dokes showed his speed early and cut the challenger near the right eye in round two. Coetzee took the punches and kept coming.

His rebuilt right hand had earned him the nickname “The Bionic Hand,” and it remained one of his best weapons. Dokes had another punch to consider that night, though: Coetzee used his left hook more often than he had in earlier title bids. The hook made his attack less predictable while he pressed the quicker champion.

In the fifth, a short left-right combination put Dokes down on one knee. He rose quickly and fought back, but the knockdown changed the terms of the fight. Coetzee did not slow down as he had against Tate and Weaver. He stayed close enough to make Dokes work and reached the tenth ahead on all three official cards. Dokes still had good moments, particularly in the eighth; this was no uncontested march to the finish.

Coetzee landed two heavy rights past the midpoint of the tenth and followed Dokes into a corner. Dokes tied him up, but after referee Tony Perez separated them, Coetzee attacked again. A left-right combination sent Dokes down. The bell rang during the count, and Perez counted him out at the official time of 3:08.

The right hand helped Coetzee win the title on his third attempt. It also broke again, requiring surgery and keeping him out of the ring for more than a year. He lost the belt to Greg Page in his first defense. Dokes later admitted that cocaine and Jack Daniel’s had been part of his preparation, but that admission does not account for Coetzee’s work over ten rounds. On a night built to celebrate Dokes, the fighter everyone thought would fade was still throwing with force at the end.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Accepts Keyshawn Davis Fight
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins agreeing to face Keyshawn Davis at welterweight exposes a massive tactical gamble that could backfire on both men. Hitchins cannot survive by running all night, while Keyshawn faces an agonizing dilemma: turn into a relentless pressure fighter or get picked apart from long range for twelve miserable rounds.

Keith Connolly admitted the cold truth to his man: this is a coin flip, yet the financial payout justifies the danger.

“We’ve accepted the fight. We’re waiting for a couple of commercial things to come through, so to speak, a date to be set. I told Hitchins, it’s a 50-50 fight. But I said, ‘This is the type of fight that if you take it, it’s worth the risk because of the money we’d be receiving, but also the opportunity of two guys fighting in their prime,’” Connolly said to Brian Custer.

Gustavo Lemos already provided the blueprint to rip Hitchins apart by refusing to let him settle into a rhythm. Keyshawn brings sharper reflexes and slicker counterpunches than Lemos, yet patience will ruin him here. Hitchins wants a slow, sleepy track meet where he can flick out light jabs and steal rounds without getting hit.

Keyshawn must trap Hitchins on the ropes, rip shots to the ribs, and fight through the inevitable clinches. Stepping into that pocket comes with severe danger. Hitchins excels at leaning on opponents, tying up arms, and forcing resets that drain an attacker’s stamina. Keyshawn cannot afford to reset every time Hitchins grabs him.

The jump to 147 pounds favors Hitchins physically. Keyshawn built his career down at lightweight, while Hitchins carries natural length and leverage that will look massive inside the ring. Keyshawn will not overpower Hitchins with size. He has to take punches to land his own, risking exhaustion against a rangy spoiler who knows how to make opponents miss.

Placing this fight on a massive Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua stadium event or a David Benavidez vs. Michal Cieslak bill is the only way promoters can afford both purses. Neither man draws enough single ticket buyers to headline on their own. Once the money is guaranteed, Keyshawn must decide if he truly has the engine to chase Hitchins down.

Ghana News.title: 2026/27 cocoa season: COCOBOD engages international trading partners in London
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive of COCOBOD, Dr. Ransford Abbey, and his Deputy in charge of Finance & Administration, Mr. Ato Boateng, held a strategic engagement with leading international cocoa trading companies in London as part of preparations for Ghana's 2026/27 cocoa season.

The meeting, convened by Ghana Cocoa Marketing Company (UK) Ltd. (GCMC UK), brought together representatives of major international cocoa trading and processing companies with longstanding commercial relationships with Ghana's cocoa sector.

The meeting formed part of COCOBOD's commitment to maintaining open dialogue with key stakeholders and ensuring that trading partners remain informed and engaged as Ghana implements reforms aimed at strengthening the sustainability, efficiency and competitiveness of its cocoa sector.

Discussions focused on the newly enacted Ghana Cocoa Board Act, 2026 (Act 1182), the proposed cocoa sector financing framework, preparations for the 2026/27 cocoa season, and other operational and commercial matters relevant to industry participants.

Key discussion areas included the proposed commercial paper and bond financing programme, liquidity arrangements for the season, the role of private-sector financing in supporting Licensed Buying Companies (LBCs), EUDR implementation readiness, and opportunities to strengthen collaboration between COCOBOD and international trading partners.

The engagement was characterised by open, constructive and forward-looking discussions.

Participants welcomed the opportunity to engage directly with COCOBOD leadership and exchange perspectives on strengthening Ghana's cocoa sector and ensuring a successful start to the new season.

COCOBOD reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, stakeholder engagement and continuous collaboration with its trading partners as implementation arrangements for the new financing framework evolve.

The meeting also reinforced the longstanding partnership between Ghana and the international cocoa trade and underscored the shared commitment to maintaining Ghana's position as a trusted and preferred origin of premium cocoa.

Ghana News.title: Fire contained at Dansoman’s Dayspring School, no casualties reported
Ghana News.content:
A fire broke out at Dayspring School in Dansoman on Thursday morning, affecting portions of the school building.

The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) says the fire is currently under control, and all pupils have been successfully evacuated to safety.

No casualties have been reported.

According to the GNFS, the Service received a distress call at the Dansoman Fire Station at about 11:00 a.m., indicating a fire outbreak at the school.

The first appliance from the Dansoman Fire Station arrived at the incident scene at 11:03 a.m. Upon assessment of the situation, firefighters requested additional support from the Industrial Area Fire Station.

Personnel from the Industrial Area Fire Station arrived at 11:15 a.m., and, together with their colleagues from Dansoman, brought the fire under control.

“We are informed that as of the time of the fire, there were students present on the premises, but thankfully the students were evacuated successfully without any harm,” the GNFS said.

The Service said the fire has been successfully confined from spreading further, and no casualties have been recorded.

“All the children are in safe hands, and personnel from both the Dansoman Fire Station and the Industrial Area Fire Station are putting their collective efforts together to ensure that the place remains safe before we disperse from here,” the GNFS added.

Investigations into the cause of the fire are expected to begin as emergency responders complete their operations at the scene.

Ghana News.title: Nyankyerenease gets furnished CHPS compound to improve healthcare access
Ghana News.content:
The Kwadaso Municipal Assembly in the Ashanti Region has commissioned and handed over a fully furnished Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) compound at Nyankyerenease to bring healthcare closer to the aged and also improve access to healthcare in the community.

The facility, funded through the Assembly’s Common Fund, is expected to ease the difficulties faced by residents, particularly the aged, who previously had to trek several miles to access basic healthcare services.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, the Kwadaso Municipal Chief Executive, Eric Assibey, reaffirmed the government’s commitment to bringing quality healthcare closer to residents and ensuring the smooth implementation of free primary healthcare.

He said the Assembly would construct additional CHPS compounds in communities where suitable lands have been made available.

“Aside from the Nyankyerenease CHPS compound, we will build others in areas where the lands are ready. If the budget allocated in the Common Fund for health is not used for its intended purpose, the authorities will question us. So, wherever there is a need for a CHPS compound in the Kwadaso Municipality, we will ensure that it is built and commissioned,” he said.

Mr. Assibey disclosed that the Assembly would soon commission additional CHPS compounds at Asuyeboah Container and Kwadaso as part of efforts to bring healthcare services closer to residents.

The Municipal Health Director for Kwadaso, Grace Billi Kampitib, also disclosed that the Nyankyerenease facility has commenced operations following its commissioning.

According to her, the facility has been provided with health personnel and essential medicines to begin serving residents, although additional equipment and logistical support are needed.

“We have staff and medicines to take care of patients who will be coming, but we need more equipment and support,” she appealed.

Mrs Kampitib further raised concerns about the increasing incidence of non-communicable diseases in the municipality and urged residents to seek medical attention regularly instead of relying on self-medication.

She also advised residents to ensure that their National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) cards remain active to enable them to access healthcare services without financial difficulties.

Some elderly residents who attended the commissioning expressed relief over the establishment of the facility, saying it would save them the stress of travelling long distances to seek medical care.

“Over the years, we have suffered by walking several miles to the hospital. But now that we have a CHPS compound here, our suffering has come to an end,” one elderly resident told Adom News.

Ghana News.title: Sky Train trial moves to defence as Asamoah, Ameyaw-Akumfi file witness statements
Ghana News.content:
The two accused persons in the ongoing Sky Train trial, former Ghana Infrastructure Investment Fund (GIIF) Chief Executive Officer Solomon Asamoah and former GIIF Board Chairman Prof Christopher Ameyaw-Akumfi, have filed their witness statements.

According to a case update posted on X, formerly Twitter, by the Deputy Attorney General, Justice Srem-Sai, the statements were filed on Wednesday, September 23, the final deadline set by the High Court for the accused to present their defence.

The development clears the way for the trial to proceed after the prosecution closed its case and the High Court dismissed Mr Asamoah’s submission of no case.

Mr Asamoah had subsequently challenged that decision at the Supreme Court and sought an injunction to prevent the High Court from continuing with the trial pending the determination of his certiorari application.

However, the Supreme Court, sitting as a single-Judge court, dismissed his application for an interlocutory injunction on August 31, 2026.

Justice Senyo Dzamefe held that Mr Asamoah’s own affidavit evidence did not disclose a serious case to be tried and that the issues he raised were matters properly within the remit of an appeal.

The Court also found that the High Court judge had acted within jurisdiction when ruling on the submission of no case and that Mr Asamoah had failed to demonstrate irreparable harm if the injunction was not granted.

Mr Asamoah and Prof Ameyaw-Akumfi are facing trial over allegations that US$2 million was paid towards the Sky Train project without the approval of the GIIF Board.

The filing of their witness statements means both accused have now formally presented their defence as the court proceedings continue.

Sports and Recreation Minister Kofi Iddie Adams is optimistic about Ghana’s 2027 African Cup of Nations opening qualifying campaign in spite of the absence of several players.

The absences includes captain Jordan Ayew, Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo, Tottenham Hotspur forward Mohammed Kudus, Thomas Partey, among others.

The Black Stars will be tested in their Group C opener against Côte d'Ivoire at the Stade de la Paix in Bouake on 24 September before facing The Gambia five days later at the Accra Sports stadium.

Ghana coach Carlos Queiroz had to hand late call-ups as replacements for the withdrawals.

Adams believes in the ability of the available players to produce good results from both fixtures.

“We are hoping that on the 24th of this month, when we got to Bouake, we are either drawing or getting all three points, and against The Gambia on the 29th to get all three points” He told Max TV.

Black Stars are hoping to return to the continental showpiece after missing out on the previous edition.

Ghana News.title: Heavy security at Accra High Court ahead of Salomey Baffoe bail hearing after EOCO’s attempted arrest of Manhyia South MP
Ghana News.content:
A heavy security presence has been observed at the Accra High Court on Thursday, September 24, ahead of the hearing of the bail application of nurse Salomey Awiti Baffoe.

The heightened security presence follows tense scenes at the court premises on Wednesday, September 23, when officials of the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) attempted to arrest Manhyia South Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah.

The incident occurred as the MP was at the court to represent Baffoe in connection with her bail application.

According to accounts of the incident, an EOCO official approached the legislator after proceedings and sought to take him into custody in connection with an ongoing investigation. The attempt resulted in a confrontation at the court premises as the MP resisted the move.

The situation attracted the attention of people at the court, with the development unfolding in full view of other lawyers.

EOCO subsequently confirmed that its officers had attempted to arrest Baffour Awuah. The agency explained that the move was connected to an investigation and that the MP had previously been invited to assist with the matter.

The incident has since added another layer of attention to proceedings involving Baffoe, whose bail application is expected to come before the High Court today.

Salomey Baffoe, a Techiman senior nurse, is facing a charge of abetment of crime in connection with an alleged false publication involving a TikToker named Barbara Asantewaa Kodua, known as “Ghana Jollof.”

She was previously remanded by the Adentan Circuit Court following her arrest and subsequent prosecution in connection with the case.

Her lawyers subsequently approached the High Court seeking her release on bail, arguing that she should be allowed to remain out of custody while the case proceeds.

The bail application came before the High Court on Wednesday, but the court adjourned proceedings after the prosecution requested more time to respond to the application.

The prosecution told the court that the Attorney-General’s Office had been served with the bail application on September 18 and needed additional time to prepare its response.

The defence, led by Member of Parliament Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, opposed the request for an adjournment. The MP argued that the application concerned the liberty of his client and should therefore be dealt with without unnecessary delay.

The court subsequently adjourned the matter, paving the way for the bail application to be considered today.
