World.title: Iraq’s Gulf Cup 27 match against Oman ends in 1-1 draw
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi and Omani national teams drew 1-1 on Wednesday in the opening match of the 27th Gulf Cup held at Prince Abdullah Al-Faisal Sports City Stadium in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Iraq launched a strong attack, causing Oman to make a defensive mistake. Zaid Ismail took advantage of the rebound and set it up for Mohammed Qasim, who fired a rocket shot with his left foot into the near corner, giving the “Lions of Mesopotamia” an early lead in the sixth minute.

The Omani team’s performance improved, and their level rose during the second half. After a decisive and skillful pass from Ahmed al-Kaabi, Nasser al-Rawahi scored the equalizer brilliantly from a close range, winning the “Man of the Match” award in recognition of his outstanding performance.

In a candid evaluation, Australian coach Graham Arnold, who manages the Iraqi national team, acknowledged that the team’s performance fell short of expectations. He pointed out that the rushed preparations had hindered the implementation of their tactical plan.

The Iraqi team only had one training session before the tournament compared to six for the Omani team.

“We were not the better side, and we must work harder in the coming matches to secure the win,” Arnold said.

The manager of the Oman team, Tarik Sektioui, expressed his great pride in his team, describing the squad as “fighters” for their ability to recover from an early setback and snatch a vital opening point against the defending champions.

World.title: Turkey to hand over military base to enhance Iraqi sovereignty
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced on Wednesday that Turkish forces will gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zelikan base to the Iraqi government.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the handover process will take place in accordance with an agreed-upon mechanism and timeline amid the progress Iraq has achieved through security measures.

During their meeting on the sideline of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, the two leaders agreed to deepen security cooperation in negotiations in which Iraqi and Turkish authorities discussed strategic relations.

Additionally, al-Zaidi and Erdogan agreed to completely expand the Iraqi state’s authority in Sinjar and to eliminate the presence of banned foreign armed groups.

Turkey established a military base in Bashiqa, near Mosul, in December 2015, initially deploying around 600 soldiers to train local forces to combat ISIS terrorist groups.

The deployment of Turkish soldiers without formal consent from Iraq has been a longstanding point of contention, often regarded as a violation of Iraq’s sovereignty and a strain on the relationship between Ankara and Baghdad.

As part of the agreement, Iraq agreed to restore state authority in Sinjar and remove or disarm foreign armed groups and militias that Turkey sees as security risks.

World.title: Iraq to raise gas production at Nahr Bin Umar to 300 million cubic feet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil revealed on Monday that it is planning to increase associated gas recovery at the Nahr Bin Umar field to 300 million cubic feet per day.

Deputy Minister for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber chaired a meeting to review associated gas recovery plans and projects at the Nahr Bin Umar field in the southern province of Basra.

The meeting was attended by representatives from the South Gas Company (SGC) and the project operator, Halfaya Gas Company, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The meeting focused on the development plan to enhance associated gas recovery, aiming for a target of 300 million standard cubic feet per day.

The plan will be implemented in two phases, each with a capacity of 150 million standard cubic feet per day.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil said earlier that the Bin Umar gas project will produce between 500 and 600 tons of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Saber mentioned earlier that the project, which will minimize gas flaring and support the country’s electricity grid, is planned to be operational by the end of April.

Saber confirmed the news while inspecting the project’s final connection point in mid-April.

The project will produce 70 million standard cubic feet per day of raw gas, between 500 and 600 tons of LPG for home consumption, around 80 million standard cubic feet per day of dry gas for power plants, and more than 1,800 barrels per day of condensates.

The initiative is an important step toward increasing gas utilization, preventing gas flaring, and strengthening the country’s electricity grid.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 3 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Tuesday that oil exports for August reached approximately 70 million barrels, with daily shipments exceeding three million barrels.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the deals the ministry reached to transport oil through the Turkish port of Ceyhan raised the volumes to 600,000 barrels per day, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Iraq’s oil exports fluctuated during September 2026, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions related to the Middle East war and Baghdad’s efforts to diversify its export routes.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that exports started at three million barrels per day at the beginning of September but have since gradually declined to about 2.4 million barrels per day at present.

Despite a decline in Iraqi oil exports during September, the figures still surpassed the average daily exports in August, which were approximately 2.35 million barrels per day. This increase was bolstered by enhanced shipping traffic and a decrease in shipping disruptions in the Gulf over the past few weeks.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

The prime minister indicated that it is important to improve infrastructure and export capacity to meet the expected rise in output.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Al-Zaidi directed an increase in output from oil fields in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the expansion of exploration activities to achieve the plan’s objectives and reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

World.title: Iraq’s exports hit $19.55 billion in Q1 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Figures released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) showed that the country’s exports reached $19.55 billion in the first quarter of 2026, compared to imports of $10.27 billion.

Hydrocarbons continued to account for the significant bulk of Iraq’s exports, exposing the country to larger global energy dynamics.

Iraq’s crude oil exports totaled $18.64 billion, petroleum products $762.2 million, and other exports $148.5 million.

The state sector’s imports totaled $1.35 billion, and the private sector’s imports reached $8.92 billion, according to the National Iraqi News Agency (NINA).

Iraq’s trade balance indicated a surplus of $10.82 billion, according to figures from the CBI that compare exports with imports.

The country’s exports during the first quarter of 2026 are lower than those of the fourth quarter of 2025, which stood at $21.62 billion.

Iraq’s export capacity during the first quarter of 2026 experienced significant headwinds due to rigorous OPEC+ production limits and interruptions related to maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Golan will remain Syrian, vows President al-Sharaa at UN
World.content:
United Nations – Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa insisted at the UN Wednesday that the Golan Heights region will remain Syrian after Colombia last month recognized Israeli sovereignty over the strategically important territory.

“Any attempts that violate our sovereignty, violate international law, will be stopped. Golan will remain Syrian territories,” al-Sharaa said at the UN meeting of world leaders in New York.

Colombia’s new hard-right government in August recognized Israel’s claim over the Golan Heights, which it captured from Syria in 1967.

The United States had until then been the only country to recognize Israel’s annexation of the territory in 1981.

The United Nations maintains that the plateau is Syrian territory under Israeli military occupation.

In July UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres reiterated that the Golan Heights were part of Syria, describing Israeli occupation as “totally unacceptable.”

Al-Sharaa also used his second turn at the UN rostrum to denounce repeated Israeli strikes on his country since the fall of former dictator Bashar al-Assad.

“Israel is launching attacks against Syria. There have been 500 air strikes, more than 1,200 incursions, and 300 detentions. This is at odds with the orientation we’re seeing at global level,” he said.

“It is reminiscent of a era that we thought was long gone.”

World.title: Iraq urges Iran to defuse regional tensions through dialogue
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein emphasized to his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, on Wednesday the importance of defusing regional tensions through dialogue.

Hussein’s remarks took place during his meeting with Araghchi in New York on the sidelines of their participation in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The meeting addressed bilateral relations and regional developments, as well as the importance of continued coordination between the two countries to respond to current challenges and support diplomatic efforts aimed at enhancing regional stability.

Hussein stressed the significance of continued diplomatic efforts among the parties involved to defuse tension, prevent escalation, and maintain regional stability.

Araghchi outlined the discussions that began between Iran and the United States, sponsored by an intermediary, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meetings in New York. These discussions attempt to de-escalate the situation and find approaches to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for navigation.

The two sides discussed the outcomes of the meeting involving the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, and Turkey—attended by US President Donald Trump—as well as how regional and international relationships might help efforts for de-escalation.

The two ministers emphasized the importance of supporting diplomatic efforts aimed at preventing escalation, defusing tensions, and fostering opportunities for dialog and peaceful solutions.

World.title: China’s Yu, 13, wins third gold with latest Asian Games record
World.content:
Tokyo – China’s 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a hat-trick of Asian Games golds on Wednesday with a dominant victory in the 400m individual medley, two years out from the Los Angeles Olympics.

The school girl powered home in an Asian Games-record 4min 28.56sec to make it a clean sweep from her three individual events in Tokyo, following victories in the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley, also in Games-record times.

She beat the previous 400m IM Games record set by China’s Ye Shiwen in 2014 by almost 4.5 seconds.

It was the fourth-fastest time in the world this year, with world record-holder Summer McIntosh owning the top three.

Yu is shaping up to be a major medal threat at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

She has been the talk of swimming since becoming the youngest medallist in world championships history last year with bronze for China’s relay team aged just 12.

She also finished just outside the medals in fourth in three world individual events.

She has embellished her growing reputation this year, notably with a victory over multiple American Olympic champion Regan Smith in March.

She has dominated this week in Tokyo and gave another glimpse of her immense talent in the 400m IM.

Yu took the lead straight from the start and set off on a procession towards the finish line.

She finished 3.95sec clear of silver medallist Ke Wenxi of China, with Japan’s Mio Narita finishing third.

As well as international news headlines, her Asian Games exploits have caused a sensation back home.

Her back story, such as being spotted by chance by a swimming coach at a water park, and her struggle with interviews, have gone viral.

Asked if answering questions was the hardest part, she replied with a giggle this week: “Every time I just want to float off somewhere else.”

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha

on Thursday took aim at the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar after reports of differences within the poll body over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls sparked a political stir.

He accused the CEC of "vote chori, kanun chori, sanstha chori (vote theft, law theft, institutional theft)", calling it an "act against nation".

He claimed that all elections were "rigged", further questioning why PM Narendra Modi and Amit Shah do not face anti-incumbency.

"The

is the institutional protector of the vote... I have shown it with proof, and there is already more than enough information to make this a 100 % certainty that Indian elections, Lok Sabha elections, 2024 election, Vidhan Sabha elections are all being rigged," he said addressing a press conference.

"I come from a political family, and I have spent more than 50 years in a political family... In India, there is a fundamental force called anti-incumbency that very quickly starts to resist any government. It does not spare anybody. Indira Gandhi won the Bangladesh war, was at the height of her popularity, and then suddenly, within a year or two, massive anti-incumbency, massive pressure," he said.

"The same exact thing happens to leader after leader after leader.





Happens to Congress leaders; it happens to regional parties, but for some reason, it never happens to Mr Narendra Modi, does not happen to Mr Shah, does not happen to the BJP," he added.

Rahul pointed out that Congress, in the past, has raised the issue of "vote chori" on several occassions but the "institutional framework of India was not interested".

"Gyanesh Kumar, two election commissioners, are raising questions on that man.

I have been raising questions. Those questions were ignored. People of India believed it. But the institutional framework of India was not interested... Gyanesh Kumar was chosen by the Prime Minister of India, not by anybody less. He was chosen by Amit Shah," he said.

"Now two election commissioners are saying that Mr Gyanesh Kumar is responsible for the chaos and the damage that has taken place to our voting system.

From vote-chori comes Kanun-chori.... From Kanun-chori comes Sanstha chori â institutions. This is the chain that has taken place..," he added.

An Indian Express report has highlighted differences among members of the EC over the SIR of electoral rolls. World.title: Delhi HC denies anticipatory bail to YouTuber Ajeet Bharti in casteist remarks case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Thursday refused to grant anticipatory bail to YouTuber Ajeet Bharti in a case over alleged casteist and derogatory remarks against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad, holding that the plea was not maintainable.

Justice Saurabh Banerjee dismissed Bhartiâs pre-arrest bail plea, saying a case under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was prima facie made out against him. The court also noted the statutory bar on granting anticipatory bail under the Act.

"In view of the fact that a case under the provisions of the SC/ST Act is prima facie made out against the applicant and considering the statutory bar (on grant of bail) under the SC/ST Act, the present petition seeking grant of anticipatory bail is dismissed being not maintainable," the judge said while pronouncing the verdict.

The detailed order is awaited.

HC hears arguments from Bharti, police and Azad

The high court had reserved its order on September 16 after hearing arguments from Bharti's counsel, the

and Azad.

Bharti had moved the high court after a Delhi trial court rejected his anticipatory bail plea on September 7. The trial court had found that the material before it prima facie disclosed the ingredients of an offence under the SC/ST Act and that the statutory bar on pre-arrest bail applied.





Bharti's counsel argued before the high court that the SC/ST Act was not attracted because there was no intentional insult or humiliation. He said the remarks should be considered in the context in which they were made.

His lawyer also argued that Bharti had not used any casteist slur and had made the remarks during an exchange on social media after what he described as serious provocation involving a family member.

The Delhi Police opposed the plea, arguing that the words allegedly used by Bharti directly insulted a particular caste.

The prosecutor said the remarks were made on a social media platform and not in a closed setting, and contended that the ingredients required to attract the SC/ST Act were present.

Azad's lawyer also opposed the anticipatory bail plea, describing the alleged remarks as derogatory and intentional.

The FIR was registered under provisions of the SC/ST Act, the Information Technology Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

The case relates to remarks allegedly made by Bharti during a programme on social media. The complaint was registered at Delhi's North Avenue police station.

World.title: Elaborate security arrangements for Ganesha procession in Shivamogga
World.content:
The immersion procession of the Ganesha idol installed by the Hindu Mahasabha will be taken out in the city on Friday, under tight security cover arranged by the district administration and police.

The event, which draws large crowds from the city and outside every year, has once again turned the spotlight on Shivamogga, with elaborate arrangements and a display of devotional and artistic fervour visible across several localities. The day-long procession, which draws massive crowds, carries added significance in the context of past instances that triggered communal tension and a spate of law-and-order cases in the city.

The procession will begin at Bheemeshwara Temple and pass through S.P.M. Road, Ramanna Shreshti Park, Gandhi Bazar Main Road, S.N. Circle, A.A. Circle, Nehru Road, Gopi Circle, Durgigudi, Jail Circle, Shivamurthy Circle, Mahaveer Circle, D.V.S. Circle, Convent Road, and Kote Road before the idol is immersed in the Tunga River near Bheemeshwara Temple.

At a press conference held in Shivamogga on Thursday, the organising committee detailed the arrangements for the event. Speaking to reporters, Shivamogga MLA S.N. Channabasappa said the Hindu Mahasabha has been installing the Ganesha idol to mark the festival for the past 82 years.

Holiday

He said several traffic circles across the city had been decorated with artistic displays depicting Hindu mythological and historical figures, and that various youth and pro-Hindu organisations had made preparations to ensure the procession passed off peacefully. Some organisations, he added, would distribute juice, sweets, and prasad to devotees taking part.

Deputy Commissioner Prabhulinga Kavilakatti has issued a notification on traffic management for the day, diverting vehicles entering and leaving the city and banning parking and vehicular movement along the entire procession route for the duration of the event. In view of the scale of the celebrations, several schools in the city have declared a holiday for Friday.

Briefing the media on the security arrangements, Shivamogga Superintendent of Police B. Nikhil said the event would be closely monitored through a large deployment of personnel, comprising over 4,500 police personnel. They include five officers of the rank of SP/Additional SP, 22 Deputy SPs, 164 inspectors, around 300 police sub-inspectors, and nearly 4,000 police staff and home guards.

He said 12 platoons of the Karnataka State Reserve Police (KSRP) and 10 District Armed Reserve platoons would be deployed, along with quick response teams, two companies of Rapid Action Force. Seven fire units and four ambulance teams will also be stationed along the route, he said, with the entire event kept under watch through CCTV cameras and mobile camera units.

The SP added that, as a precautionary measure, the police had already registered nearly 900 preventive cases and externed around 35 persons.

World.title: Amid heavy rain, overall reservoir levels hold steady at 50% in Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
Heavy rains over the past one-and-a-half days under the influence of a depression have not altered storage levels significantly in Andhra Pradesh’s major dams and barrages. As of September 24, the State’s reservoirs held 552.81 TMC against their combined capacity of 1,106.36 TMC — about 50%. While the Godavari and Krishna river systems witnessed substantial inflows, key reservoirs in the Pennar basin and Rayalaseema remained well below capacity, reflecting the uneven distribution of water across the State.

Over the past 24 hours, storage levels across the five major dams and barrages remained virtually flat, with releases being regulated according to inflows and downstream conditions. The stability in storage levels came despite substantial movement of water through parts of the Godavari and Krishna systems.

The Godavari basin continued to receive heavy flows. The Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage at Dowleswaram recorded an inflow and outflow of 1,37,099 cusecs. The barrage, with a capacity of 2.93 TMC, recorded no change in storage during the last 24 hours, with the incoming flow being passed downstream, WRD officials say.

At the Donkarayi Reservoir, the inflow and outflow were both 3,485 cusecs, with storage remaining unchanged.

In the Krishna basin, the Srisailam dam had 95.36 TMC against its 215.81 TMC capacity. No instant inflow was recorded, while the downstream release was maintained at 7,250 cusecs. There was no change in storage during the period, the officials say.

At Nagarjuna Sagar, storage increased marginally from 180.09 TMC to 180.10 TMC. The reservoir received an inflow of 6,051 cusecs and released 6,027 cusecs. Its storage stood at about 58% of its 312.05 TMC capacity.

Further downstream, the Pulichinthala project in Palnadu district had 27.45 TMC against its 45.77 TMC capacity, with the water level at 161.61 feet. The project received an inflow of 3,688 cusecs and released 400 cusecs. Its storage remained unchanged over the 24 hour period.

At Prakasam Barrage in NTR district, the inflow and outflow were both recorded at 11,588 cusecs. The barrage recorded no change in its reported storage of 3.03 TMC, officials say.

Large unfilled capacity

The storage position in the Pennar basin and Rayalaseema remained considerably lower. The Somasila Reservoir held 16.50 TMC against its 78 TMC capacity, leaving 61.50 TMC of available capacity. The Kandaleru Reservoir had 17.27 TMC against its 68.03 TMC capacity, leaving 50.76 TMC of available capacity.

The combined storage reported for the Rayalaseema region was 171.62 TMC against a total capacity of 372.37 TMC, leaving 200.75 TMC of unfilled capacity.

The contrasting storage positions underline the uneven distribution of water across the State. While the Godavari and Krishna systems are handling substantial flows, reservoirs in the Pennar basin and Rayalaseema continue to remain well below their full-reservoir levels.

World.title: Lake renovation panel launches plantation drive in Thanjavur district
World.content:
A drive to plant one lakh palmyra tree seeds around Senkazhuneer lake in Thanjavur district was launched on Thursday.

The drive, to be implemented through the Senkazhuneer Lake Renovation Committee, was inaugurated by Collector R. Revathi.

The over 1,000-year-old Chola-period lake spread of over 642 acres to the west of Kallaperambur in the district had been identified for planting the palm tree seeds though the National Service Scheme and voluntary organisations, an official press release said.
