The Misaktsieli school continued to spend money on various works and services in 2026. Its most recent contract, signed on 4 September, was worth 12,515 lari [about $4,635] and covered the removal of flooring, plumbing work and the subsequent installation of granite flooring.

The school in the village of Abranlo, in the Kvemo Kartli region, is the smallest of the schools closed in recent days, with around 80 pupils. It too has undergone renovation work in recent years.

Mariko Tsikoridze, a project co-ordinator for CENN in Kvemo Kartli, says three sanitation and hygiene projects were carried out at the school before 2019. Toilets were built, washbasins renovated, and an illegal rubbish dump created by local residents in the school grounds was cleared.

“We brought in six truckloads of soil and built a sports ground. The local authorities were also actively involved at the time,” Tsikoridze says.

The school is now due to be demolished. Its headteacher, Mikheil Jakeli, wrote on social media that, according to the National Forensics Bureau’s assessment, constructing a new building would be preferable to repairing the existing one, prompting the ministry to decide on demolition.

Problems left unaddressed

For some of the schools, JAMnews was unable to find any relevant records in the public procurement system. However, municipal reports and local media articles show that concerns about the condition of these schools had been raised for years.

For example, parents of pupils at Public School No 5 in Khashuri were calling for repairs as early as January 2023, complaining about damaged walls, floors and doors, as well as loose stair railings.

First day of the new academic year at Public School No 5 in Khashuri. Photo: school’s official Facebook page.

In municipal reports from the Imereti region, Public School No 2 in Tskaltubo had for years been listed as a building in need of renovation.

Available records for 2022-2026 contain no evidence of major renovation work at the school. However, according to Info Imereti, minor repairs were carried out, including in the summer of 2026.

“There is an assessment stating that the building is not cost-effective to repair. It would therefore be better to construct a new one rather than renovate it,” Mamuka Chkhetiani, head of the Tskaltubo education resource centre, told Kutaisi Post.

Officials knew as early as 2022-2023 that Public School No 3 in Senaki was in a state of disrepair. In 2022, the school’s headteacher, Marine Naneishvili, told Etaloni that the building was due to be demolished.

The Finance Ministry’s 2023 review of investment projects listed the “Construction of Public School No 3 in Senaki”as a separate project, with 12.696m lari [about $4.7m] allocated for it. It is unclear what became of the project.

Public School No 3 in Senaki. Photo: school’s official Facebook page.

Reaction at schools

Members of the school communities at two of the 10 schools — in Tbilisi and Misaktsieli — responded to the authorities’ decision with protests, which are still continuing. At the other schools, discontent has largely been confined to social media, where parents have complained about the disruption to both their children’s plans and their own.

“We are in shock” is the most common reaction beneath posts announcing each new school closure.

Two of the three schools closed in the Kakheti region — Public School No 3 in Gurjaani and the school in the village of Velistsikhe — are in Gurjaani municipality. More than 500 children attend the Velistsikhe school, while School No 3 has 148 pupils.

“Congratulations to the school community of Velistsikhe Public School — pupils, parents, teachers and everyone interested in improving our school,” headteacher Nona Menabdishvili wrote on social media alongside the news of its closure.

The post attracted numerous comments, many of them essentially asking: “What is there to celebrate?” Others shared stories of schools elsewhere that have remained closed for years.

Unlike Menabdishvili, Mikheil Jakeli, headteacher of the school in Abranlo, expressed no enthusiasm about the Education Ministry’s decision.

He has appealed to the ministry to allow pupils to complete the current academic year in the old building, subject to appropriate safety measures, “to avoid moving the children elsewhere just days after the start of classes and causing them unnecessary stress”.

‘From positive assessment to demolition’ – story of School No 21

The largest of the 10 schools to be closed is Public School No 21 in Tbilisi, formerly Gymnasium No 6. News of its closure was also the first to emerge.

It is one of the capital’s most prestigious schools. Because of its emphasis on German-language teaching, it is often referred to as the “German school”.

According to a National Forensics Bureau assessment dated 10 September 2026, several problems were identified in the school building, including a risk of plaster falling from the façade, a faulty drainage system, cracks in some areas and damage to reinforced concrete blocks.

The assessment also identified seismic vulnerability as a separate problem, citing the absence of an earthquake-resistant reinforcement belt on the roof parapet and other failures to comply with current seismic standards.

Protest outside Public School No 21 on 18 September 2026. “Don’t demolish the Sixth,” reads an improvised protest banner.

However, the same school had previously received a very different assessment from the same National Forensics Bureau on 15 November 2023, when it underwent authorisation. The assessment said the building required repairs, but gave it an overall “positive” evaluation, and the school was authorised to operate until 2032.

In April 2026, the Authorisation Council carried out scheduled monitoring of the school and, citing the positive assessment, said the building required repairs and gave the school until 2028 to address the problems.

In other words, as recently as spring 2026, official documents still listed School No 21 as requiring repairs rather than demolition.

However, by the time the Authorisation Council made that assessment, a new examination of the school building was already under way.

The Municipal Development Fund had requested the examination on 16 September 2025. An expert inspected the building on 10 December, and nine months later, on 10 September 2026, issued a new assessment.

The building was initially classified as Category III based on the extent of the damage. However, following Georgian government decree No 161 of 22 April 2026, which sets out criteria for assessing whether buildings are fit for use, the damage was subsequently classified as Category IV because of seismic safety concerns.

How could the school have deteriorated so severely in three years that it now needs to be demolished? This is the question being asked by parents. Many suspect corruption. The school is located in a prestigious tourist area, prompting speculation that a private investor may be interested in the site.

Parents fear that the school will be demolished and never rebuilt. They are demanding an independent assessment and say they will not allow the building to be torn down. They also oppose both online learning and the relocation of pupils to other schools.

If we don’t act now, we will lose our school’ – story of Misaktsieli village school

Protest outside the school in Misaktsieli, 18 September 2026.

Irine Kalandadze’s child started first grade this year. He had barely had time to settle into school when his parents were told it was closing:

“He had only been at school for three days and was eagerly looking forward to the next one — he liked it so much. Then suddenly we were told the school was closing. I can’t explain this to my child, and it is very painful for me too. This is precisely the stage when children need to develop a love of school, and now we don’t even know where or how he will study.”

The school in Misaktsieli serves five villages in Mtskheta municipality and has more than 500 pupils.

Parents say lessons will be held online for the first week after the closure, after which the children will be transferred to the school in the village of Tsilkani. But that school has capacity for only 300 pupils, meaning classes will have to be held in several shifts.

Parents do not know for certain whether the Misaktsieli school is due to be demolished or is being closed for repairs. On 18 September, residents gathered in the school grounds and demanded an explanation from the headteacher, who told them that he had not yet seen the expert assessment himself.

Villagers fear there may also be business interests behind the decision: the school is in a popular tourist area, occupies a large site and is surrounded by numerous commercial properties.

“We all want our children to study in a modern school. It’s just that we have seen many examples of how school renovation projects have ended,” Irine says.

Parents are demanding that, if the school needs repairs, the work be postponed until spring. If the building is to be demolished, they want construction of a new school to begin simultaneously on vacant land nearby, with the existing building demolished only once its replacement is ready.

“If we don’t act now, we will lose our school,” Irine says.

The protest is continuing, and parents say they have no intention of backing down.

Not an exception, but a wider trend

According to Georgia’s National Statistics Office, there are 2,086 state schools in the country.

In 2022, the Education Ministry launched a large-scale reconstruction programme that was intended to cover 800 schools.

Since then, hundreds of schools have closed across Georgia. Two years ago, in 2024, the fact-checking platform FactCheck reported that 21,203 pupils had been relocated to alternative premises.

Based on publicly available data, the number is likely still in the tens of thousands. The Municipal Development Fund, which oversees school reconstruction, regularly publishes updates on the completion or launch of work at schools across Georgia.

For example, in August 2026, the fund announced tenders for the reconstruction of 11 schools. None of the 10 schools closed in recent days appears on that list, suggesting that the overall number of schools currently not operating in their own buildings is considerably higher.

On 18 September, as thousands of teachers, pupils and parents were reeling from the news that their schools were being closed, government officials were holding a high-profile ceremony to reopen the renovated Public Schools No 4 and No 5 in Batumi.

Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, Education Minister Givi Mikanadze and other senior officials at the opening of two schools in Batumi. Photo: Municipal Development Fund.

What is actually happening?

Education experts say the situation illustrates systemic problems and a lack of a consistent strategy and long-term vision in the education system.

Education expert Revaz Abkhazava lists the problems created by what he describes as a poorly planned intervention — the reconstruction of schools:

It has disrupted the education process;

It has upended established routines for parents and children, including attendance at after-school clubs and additional classes;

It has shown a complete disregard for teachers’ needs, with low salaries forcing many to work at several schools at the same time;

It has imposed additional costs on the state for transporting pupils to other schools.

“The education system is extremely complex. It consists of many interconnected components. If you fail to see it as a whole, you get what we are seeing now. A single decision does not simply create one problem — it can push the entire system to the brink of collapse.”

Abkhazava says such decisions are the result of experienced and qualified professionals with institutional knowledge being pushed out of the education system.

“School reconstruction is a technical task. It does not require any special expertise. Education management professionals could have resolved this issue very easily.”

The expert also points to problems in communication between state institutions. The process, he says, was not managed in a way that would have ensured the assessments were ready at least a month before the start of the academic year.

Revaz Abkhazava believes the root of these problems lies in the politicisation of Georgia’s education system. He says education should not serve any political party and that safeguards are needed to ensure this, including an education council and teachers’ associations. He also argues that the ministry’s strategy should not change every time a new minister takes office.

“The education system should be as decentralised as possible. The ministry should employ professionals with knowledge and experience in education management and education policy.

“The ministry should focus on evaluation, analysis and research, and make decisions based on them. It should support educational institutions, while those institutions should have the autonomy to make decisions on matters that concern them,” the expert concludes.

World.title: Armenian orphanage worker brutally assaults disabled resident
World.content:
Armenian orphanage worker assaults disabled child

A care worker at the Kharberd specialised orphanage in Armenia brutally assaulted a disabled child who is unable to walk or speak.

The Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, which oversees the institution, confirmed the incident and said it had taken place several weeks ago. The care worker was immediately dismissed and is now under house arrest.

“A disabled child was beaten with a mop in a place where they were supposed to receive care and support. In reality, this is the kind of care the child needs to be protected from,” said Mushegh Hovsepyan, head of the NGO Disability Rights Agenda.

Rights activist questions purpose of such institutions

“If we do not want violence, these institutions should not exist at all. Family-based upbringing and alternative forms of care are possible for all children if the state makes the necessary effort and allocates the necessary resources. The state’s obligations do not begin after a disabled child has been beaten, nor do they end with the dismissal of the alleged abuser or their placement under house arrest,” Hovsepyan said.

Until such institutions cease to exist, however, he says the state is obliged to establish a system that:

“prevents violence and identifies signs of it in a timely manner;

provides safe mechanisms enabling all children to report abuse;

guarantees a proper investigation and the child’s swift recovery.”

Details of the incident

Local media have established further details about what happened at the orphanage. The incident is now known to have taken place on 13 August.

The child who was assaulted has cerebral palsy and is unable to walk independently or speak.

The care worker who assaulted the child had worked at the orphanage since September 2012.

“In room D-1 of the orphanage, the care worker initially struck the resident, F.M., several times. After he fell to the floor, she picked up a floor mop and continued striking him on his lower back, spine and left shoulder blade. As a result, F.M. suffered severe physical pain and emotional distress,” journalists reported.

Child’s condition described as satisfactory

Nver Kostanyan, spokesman for the minister of labour and social affairs, wrote on social media that the orphanage administration had “identified the incident” and immediately reported it to law enforcement:

“The care worker has been dismissed, while it is for law enforcement agencies to determine whether criminal charges are warranted. The child is in good health and continues to receive care at the specialised orphanage.”

Kostanyan said such incidents were a “red line” for the ministry:

“Any instance of violence is unacceptable and will be subject to an appropriate criminal-law assessment.”

Expert opinion

Mushegh Hovsepyan, head of the NGO Disability Rights Agenda, warns that disabled children often avoid speaking about abuse they have experienced.

“There are many reasons. Among other things, they think they will not be believed, because what they say is often called into question,” he wrote on Facebook.

Hovsepyan stressed that the public only learnt about the abuse at the orphanage after it was reported by the media. The rights activist believes such cases should be closely scrutinised by state bodies, particularly now that there is no mechanism for public oversight.

A group of civil society experts previously operated at the initiative of the Labour Ministry, carrying out regular monitoring of care centres for children and elderly people.

“The monitoring group was disbanded about three years ago. Easily. But its work is not being resumed with the same ease,” Hovsepyan said.

Hovsepyan himself was a member of the group. He recalls that in 2021 it visited the Kharberd specialised orphanage and documented a case of discrimination against a minor in its care:

“At the same orphanage, staff wore gloves when touching a teenager living with HIV who had recently been transferred there. Separate dishes were used for him. His clothes were washed separately. Other children were told to stay away from him. And yet the world has long known that HIV is not transmitted through this kind of contact.”

The orphanage staff themselves told the experts about this because they believed they were ‘doing everything right’.

Following the recent violent assault, Hovsepyan says he is not convinced that conditions at the specialised institution have improved:

“I am also not sure whether all new employees receive the necessary training before they start working with children. Nor am I sure that the state is taking steps to ensure that children are in safe hands.”

World.title: Series of meetings held as part of AFEZ delegation’s business visit to Malaysia (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 24. A series of high-level meetings were held as part of the business visit to Malaysia by the delegation of the Alat Free Economic Zone Authority, led by Mr. Valeh Alasgarov, Chairman of the Board of the AFEZ Authority.

As part of the visit, a meeting was held with representatives of POS Aviation, during which discussions focused on the new international airport currently under construction within the Alat Free Economic Zone and its future operations. The parties discussed the airport’s potential role in air cargo transportation and opportunities for cooperation in this area. Representatives of POS Aviation were also provided with detailed information on the activities, development plans and infrastructure of the Alat Free Economic Zone.

The delegation also met with Mr. Samer Elesawi, Chairman of the Islamic Development Bank Center of Excellence. During the meeting, Mr. Elesawi highly praised the organization of the Islamic Development Bank Group Annual Meeting held in Baku earlier this year. The parties exchanged information on the activities of the Alat Free Economic Zone and the Islamic Development Bank. Representatives of the Islamic Development Bank expressed their interest in cooperation with AFEZ and noted that investors from the organization’s member countries would be informed about the opportunities offered by the Alat Free Economic Zone.

As part of the visit, a meeting was also held with Mr. S. Jai Shankar, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (MATRADE). During the meeting, detailed information was provided on the activities of the Alat Free Economic Zone, the favorable conditions created for investors and the investment opportunities available within AFEZ. The opportunities presented were received with interest by MATRADE, which noted that Malaysian investors would be provided with further information on the investment opportunities offered by the AFEZ.

Special Event Dedicated to the Alat Free Economic Zone Held in Kuala Lumpur

On 22 September, a special event dedicated to the Alat Free Economic Zone was held in Kuala Lumpur. The event brought together high-level representatives of Malaysian government and business entities, business associations, chambers of commerce and industry, as well as companies operating across various sectors.

The event opened with remarks by H.E. Mr. Khazar Farhadov, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Azerbaijan to Malaysia. The Ambassador provided an overview of the existing cooperation between Azerbaijan and Malaysia and the prospects for further development of economic and trade relations between the two countries, highlighting the role of the Alat Free Economic Zone and the opportunities it offers in this context.

Mr. Valeh Alasgarov, Chairman of the Board of the Alat Free Economic Zone Authority, then delivered a comprehensive presentation on AFEZ. The presentation provided detailed information on AFEZ’s strategic geographical location, unique legal framework, package of fiscal and non-fiscal incentives, ready-to-use industrial land plots with ready-to-use infrastructure and utilities, services provided through the “one-stop shop” principle, and other investment opportunities.

At the conclusion of the presentation, Mr. Alasgarov invited representatives of the Malaysian business community to take advantage of the opportunities offered by the Alat Free Economic Zone and establish export-oriented manufacturing facilities within AFEZ. He also responded to questions raised by the participants.

World.title: Ferro-Alloy Resources, US Maglut sign MoU for rare earth supply from Kazakhstan
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 24. Ferro-Alloy Resources Limited (FAR), a vanadium producer and developer of the Balasausqandiq vanadium deposit in southern Kazakhstan, has signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MoU) with US rare earths separation company Maglut Heavy Industries Inc. for the potential supply of mixed rare earth concentrate (MREC) from Balasausqandiq ore, the company said.

Under the MoU, FAR could supply Maglut with up to 1,000 tons of MREC per year as a by-product of vanadium processing at the planned Balasausqandiq project.

The companies are also evaluating an intermediate project at FAR's existing operation that could produce up to 100 tons of MREC per year, subject to confirmation of its economic viability.

The MREC would be recovered from residual leach solutions generated after vanadium extraction. This could allow FAR to recover additional value from the same ore stream without changing the core vanadium processing flowsheet.

Initial test work by Maglut on a Balasausqandiq ore sample indicated the potential to separate all 16 rare earth elements (REEs) present in the sample, including yttrium, neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium.

Purities of more than 99% were achieved for the economically important REEs within two separation stages. The average overall recovery during the separation process was approximately 91.4%, while around 90.25% recovery was achieved in a single precipitation and calcination step to produce rare earth oxides.

FAR said the test work was aimed at assessing the technical potential of Maglut's separation platform and was not optimized for Balasausqandiq material. Further test work, process optimization, engineering and economic evaluation will be required.

Maglut has developed a proprietary chromatography-based platform for separating and refining high- and ultra-high-purity rare earth elements, including yttrium, neodymium and dysprosium, for the US market.

The proposed initial supply term under the MoU is five years from first production, with options for successive five-year terms. The MREC specification and pricing mechanism have yet to be agreed, while all commercial, technical and other terms remain subject to definitive agreements.

FAR said it is discussing the next phase of test work and optimization with Maglut and US strategic partners, including potential financing support for this work and the Balasausqandiq vanadium project.

The company has also commissioned SRK Consulting (UK) Limited to update its existing mineral resource estimate for Ore-Body 1 at the Balasausqandiq deposit. The initial update will include yttrium, while other REEs could be incorporated later if a limited-scope assay program currently being conducted by Intertek Minerals proves successful.

FAR previously said that historical assays had confirmed the presence of REEs in Balasausqandiq ore. Based on grades from its 2012 drilling campaign, the company estimated the in-situ value of yttrium alone in Ore-Body 1 at around $3.6 billion over the life of mine, or approximately $110 per ton of ore treated.

FAR stressed that this figure represents an in-situ value only and does not account for metallurgical recovery, operating costs or downstream processing. It should not be considered an estimate of revenue, cash flow or project value.

FAR CEO Nick Bridgen said the agreement with Maglut could position Balasausqandiq as a potential source of rare earths supply outside China.

"Securing reliable, non-Chinese supply of REEs has become a strategic priority for the United States and its allies. This MoU with Maglut is an important step in positioning Balasausqandiq as a potential future contributor to that supply chain, alongside our core vanadium business.

What makes this opportunity particularly attractive is its simplicity. The REEs would be recovered from the leach solutions that our planned vanadium process already generates, offering the potential for additional value from the same ore stream without altering the core flowsheet," Bridgen said.

He added that Maglut's initial test work had shown high purities and strong indicative recoveries, while further work would be needed to optimize the process and assess its economic viability.

FAR said the MoU is non-binding and does not guarantee that definitive agreements will be signed, that the intermediate project will proceed or that REE production will be achieved.

Listed on both the London Stock Exchange and the Astana International Exchange, Ferro-Alloy Resources Limited is a Guernsey-registered company that, through its wholly owned subsidiaries, holds the rights to explore, develop and exploit the Balasausqandiq vanadium deposit in the Kyzylorda Region of southern Kazakhstan.

Balasausqandiq is a two-phase vanadium project with significant by-products, targeting a planned annual output of 22,400 tonnes of vanadium pentoxide.

World.title: AzerGold announces its key targets for operations through 2030
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 24. AzerGold CJSC has announced its key targets for operations through 2030, the Chairman of the Executive Board of AzerGold, Zakir Ibrahimov, said at a briefing held today, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

“Over the past 10 years, AzerGold has evolved from a company focused solely on gold production into a diversified national mining company covering geological exploration, non-ferrous and ferrous metal ores, industrial explosives and non-metallic resources. By 2030, AzerGold will become a state-owned company with annual turnover reaching 1 billion manat ($588.2 million),” he said.

Ibrahimov noted that the company aims to become one of the leading companies in Azerbaijan’s non-oil industry in terms of revenue and employment.

“Environmental safety is one of the most important issues related to the development of the mining industry. As a state-owned company, AzerGold considers this approach one of the fundamental principles of our operations,” he emphasized.

According to him, the application of modern environmental standards, minimizing the environmental impact of production processes and land reclamation measures will be taken into account in the development and implementation of new projects.

Ibrahimov said that the discovery of new deposits, more efficient use of existing resources and conversion of mineral raw materials into higher value-added products will be among the main areas of focus in the coming period.

“This marks both the beginning of AzerGold’s next stage of development and a key challenge facing Azerbaijan’s mining industry as a whole,” the chairman of the board added.

World.title: AzerGold sets new deposits and expanded mining chain as key priorities
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 24. Azerbaijan’s AzerGold CJSC has identified bringing new deposits into economic circulation and expanding the mining and processing chain as among its key priorities for the coming period, the Chairman of the Executive Board of AzerGold, Zakir Ibrahimov, said at a briefing held today, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

He said the results achieved in recent years demonstrate that the necessary foundation and institutional experience have been established for the development of a modern mining industry in Azerbaijan.

“Based on the results we have achieved over these years, we can say that, thanks to the state’s attention to and support for this sector, a foundation and institutional experience have already been established for implementing the State Program and expanding Azerbaijan’s modern mining industry. Over 10 years, AzerGold has significantly expanded its production, output and revenue potential by discovering two new gold deposits, commissioning four gold mines and one regional industrial complex, and developing new areas of activity.

“As a result of the company’s operations during this period, 2.3 billion manat ($1.3 billion) in revenue has been generated for the country’s economy, and 267.2 million manat ($157.1 million) in tax payments have been made to the state budget as of August this year. During this period, the company generated a total of 618 million manat ($363.5 million) in profit. Based on its financial results for 2025, approximately 42 million manat ($24.7 million) of the profit is expected to be transferred to the state budget as dividends.

These results demonstrate AzerGold’s contribution to the development of the country’s non-oil industry, expansion of export potential, generation of state budget revenues and creation of economic value as a whole,” the AzerGold chairman emphasized.

According to Ibrahimov, the State Program marks the beginning of a new stage of activity for AzerGold while also creating an opportunity to apply the experience accumulated over the past decade on a broader scale. “Our main tasks in the coming stage are to bring new deposits into economic circulation, expand the mining and processing chain, and create greater added value within the country,” he added.

Ibrahimov said AzerGold has been designated as a key implementing body for a number of important priorities in line with its areas of activity under the Action Plan of the State Program.

He noted that the company aims not only to maintain its current development momentum but also to make new contributions to the development of the mining sector. “As AzerGold, we clearly see the responsibilities before us at this new stage. Our main goal in the coming period is not only to maintain the current development momentum but also to make new contributions to the development of the sector we represent,” the chairman of the board said.

World.title: Azerbaijan's AzerGold to invest $2.1B in four strategic mining projects
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 24. As part of the State Program, AzerGold CJSC is implementing four strategic projects with a total investment of approximately 3.63 billion manat ($2.1 billion), the Chairman of the Executive Board of AzerGold CJSC, Zakir Ibrahimov, said at a briefing held today, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

According to him, these projects include the “Soyudlu” gold mining project in the Kalbajar District, the “Ortakend” gold mining project in Nakhchivan, the “Filizchay” polymetallic project in Balakan, and the “Dashkesan” iron ore project.

“The total investment in these projects amounts to approximately 3.63 billion manat ($2.1 billion), and the total economic value is 60.4 billion manat ($35.5 billion). As is well known, mining and metallurgical projects require large capital investments and long-term financing. The President also noted at the meeting that, alongside government investments in this sector, opportunities to attract local and foreign private capital should be expanded,” Z. Ibrahimov said.

He noted that “AzerGold” plans to finance its strategic projects primarily through its own revenues and borrowed funds.

“At the same time, we are considering the possibility of attracting private and foreign investors, especially for large and capital-intensive projects. The projects I have listed will be financed through the company’s own and borrowed funds, the state budget, and contributions from potential investors. Only 10% of the funding will come from the state budget,” the chairman emphasized.

Ibrahimov reported that the first project to begin production, in chronological order, will be the Soyudlu gold deposit in Kalbajar.

“The project’s operational period, starting in 2028, is expected to last 9 years, with gold reserves of 1.03 million ounces, an economic value of 7.5 billion manat ($4.4 billion), and required investments of 425 million manat ($250.04 million). The project will be financed through AzerGold’s own and borrowed funds,” he said.

Noting that the second project is the Ortakend gold deposit located in Nakhchivan, Ibrahimov stated that production is expected to begin in 2029.

“The project’s operational life is 9 years, with gold reserves of 246,000 ounces, an economic value of 1.8 billion manat ($1.1 billion), and required investments of 255 million manat ($150.02 million). The project will be financed using AzerGold’s own funds and borrowed capital,” the chairman of the board of directors stated.

According to him, the addition of approximately 1.28 million ounces of gold reserves through the “Soyudlu” and “Ortakend” projects will enable the country to increase gold production and exports.

Production at the Filizchay deposit is scheduled to begin in 2031–2032. The chairman of the board of AzerGold stated that production at the Filizchay polymetallic deposit is scheduled to begin in 2031–2032.

“Over the 34-year operating period, we plan to produce 363,000 metric tons of copper, 2.7 million metric tons of zinc, and 1 million metric tons of lead. The project’s economic value is 29.7 billion manat ($17.4 billion), and the required investment is 1 billion manat ($590 million),” Z. Ibrahimov noted.

He reported that during the initial phase of the “Filizchay” project, AzerGold will hold 100% ownership of the deposit.

“It was emphasized that as operations progress, the economic value of the deposit will grow, and then, if necessary, the involvement of foreign investors in the project on a certain equity basis may be considered,” the chairman added.

According to Ibrahimov, the implementation of the “Filizchay” project will create new export opportunities and conditions for the development of a new industrial sector in the country.

“At the same time, this will give impetus to the region’s socioeconomic development, the creation of new jobs, and the formation of related industries around the mining sector. The project’s implementation will also create new opportunities for local contractors and service providers working in manufacturing and processing, as well as logistics and other service sectors, to expand their operations,” he said.

The chairman of the board of directors also announced that production at the Dashkesan iron ore project is scheduled to begin in 2030.

“The project, which includes mining, beneficiation, pipeline, pelletizing, and hot-briquetted iron ore (HBI) plants, plans to produce 40 million metric tons of HBI products over 20 years of operation. The project’s economic value is 24 billion manat ($14.1 billion), and the required investment is 1.95 billion manat ($1.1 billion). Funding will be provided through the state budget, borrowed funds, and investor participation,” Z. Ibrahimov said.

According to him, the ore mined at the Dashkesan mine as part of the project will first be processed at a concentrator to be built on the mine site and turned into concentrate.

“The concentrate will then be transported to a plant planned for construction in the Shamkir region for the production of pellets. To this end, plans are in place to construct a slurry pipeline over 40 kilometers long, the first of its kind in the country. In the final stage of the production chain, the pellets will be used to produce hot-briquetted iron, one of the main raw materials for the steel industry,” he noted.

Moreover, Ibrahimov reported that the plant, with an annual production capacity of 2 million metric tons, will be built in the section of the Western Industrial Park (Garb Senaye Park) located in the Shamkir region.

“The implementation of this project will help establish a sustainable raw materials base in the country for the production of high-quality steel. Annual production of 2 million metric tons will meet the needs of the domestic market, and any surplus will be exported. This will help, on the one hand, reduce dependence on imports and, on the other hand, expand export potential, develop the non-resource sector, and generate additional revenue for the state budget,” the chairman of the board of directors of AzerGold emphasized.

World.title: Azerbaijan's AzerGold сonducts preliminary exploration of five deposits in its portfolio - official
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 24. Azerbaijan’s AzerGold CJSC is conducting preliminary exploration of five deposits in its portfolio, the Chairman of the Executive Board of AzerGold, Zakir Ibrahimov, said at a briefing held today, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

According to him, the company carries out large-scale geological research and exploration in the country in order to expand the mineral resource base.

He pointed out that geological surveys covering an area of 15,000 square kilometers are currently being conducted at the expense of the state budget.

"Geological surveys covering an area of 15,000 square kilometers are currently underway at the initial exploration and assessment stage, funded by the state budget, with completion scheduled for 2027. As a result, the country's mineral resource potential—including that of the territories liberated from occupation—will be mapped," Ibrahimov explained.

He noted that there are currently 10 promising gold-copper sites at the exploration and assessment stage, and the evaluation of their resources is ongoing. This process is also expected to conclude in 2027.

The Chairman of the Board of AzerGold also touched upon geological activities planned for the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic.

"Intensive preparations are currently underway for initial exploration and assessment activities within the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic; these are being carried out by a joint venture planned under an agreement signed some time ago with the UAE-based company 'International Resources Holding'," he added.

World.title: Azerbaijan to implement per-capita financing principle at state schools
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 24. A per-capita funding principle will be implemented in the state schools of Azerbaijan.

In this regard, the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev, has signed a decree on the implementation of a new funding mechanism in state general education institutions.

The text of the document has been published on the official website of the President of Azerbaijan.

According to the decree, starting from the 2026–2027 academic year, funding for state general education institutions from the state budget will be carried out in stages based on the per-capita funding principle.

For state general education institutions subject to per-capita funding, a growth coefficient—based on the specific level of general education—will be applied to the annual education cost per student, calculated according to the type of institution.

The Cabinet of Ministers of Azerbaijan must:

- approve the rules determining the amount of annual education expenses per student—categorized by the type of state general education institution funded based on the per-capita financing principle—as well as the procedures for funding such institutions from the state budget and applying growth coefficients to the per-student annual education expense amounts based on the specific levels of general education; and report thereon to the President of Azerbaijan within one month.

- resolve other matters arising from this decree.

The Ministry of Science and Education of Azerbaijan shall determine, in coordination with the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the list of state general education institutions to be funded based on the per-capita financing principle using state budget funds, as well as the number of students in such institutions, for each subsequent calendar year.

The Ministry of Finance of Azerbaijan must ensure the financing—from state budget funds—of measures arising from the implementation of this decree.

World.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua boxing megafight announced
World.content:
A long-awaited boxing match between British former heavyweight world champions Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua has been confirmed for December 11 in Cardiff, according to an event promoter.

The two boxers will meet at the Principality Stadium, promoter Turki Alalshikh said on social media on Thursday.

Earlier media reports had suggested promoters were initially proposing to stage the fight at New York's Madison Square Garden.

The long-awaited fight has been anticipated for more than a decade. (Reuters: Supplied/Action Images/Andrew Couldridge)

“For 15 years no one has been able to make this fight,” he posted on X.

" I can now confirm that Fury Vs Joshua will be coming to the UK, as I promised British boxing fans. The time for talking is over… "

A clash between the British rivals has been one of the most anticipated fights for more than a decade.

Fury and Joshua ruled the heavyweight division for much of the past decade, but a bout between them to unify all the major belts never came to fruition.

Both were later beaten by Oleksandr Usyk, who became the undisputed heavyweight champion.

In an Instagram post on Thursday, local time, Joshua's announcement of the fight and message to fans was short: "I am inspiring a generation."

Fury stepped out of retirement this year and made his return to the ring for the first time in more than a year with victories against Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach.

Joshua’s only fights since losing his IBF world title fight against Daniel Dubois in 2024 were against YouTuber Jake Paul and Kristian Prenga.

Mr Alalshikh is a Saudi Arabian adviser who organises boxing events for the Middle Eastern kingdom.

While Fury and Joshua are arguably past their peak, it is a fight that is still likely to garner global attention and will be streamed worldwide on Netflix.

“THE WAIT IS OVER. Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua finally collide,” Joshua's promoter Matchroom posted on X.

Matchroom's Eddie Hearn told The Independent last month they had insisted on the fight taking place in the United Kingdom.

"We don’t want the money, we’d rather it was in the UK," he said.

AP

World.title: Boy, 11, dies days after being shot in the head at Sydney home
World.content:
An 11-year-old boy has died after allegedly being shot in the face at a Norwest unit in Sydney's north-west.

Police were called to the scene at about 5 pm on Monday and found the boy had sustained a gunshot wound to his face and neck.

Loading...

The boy was treated by paramedics and taken to hospital in a critical condition.

NSW Police said he died around 8 pm on Thursday.

Five other people were in the unit on Monday but were not injured.

Three 18-year-olds were arrested by police but two were later released pending further inquiries.

The third, Isaac Bechara, has been charged with concealing a serious indictable offence and remains before the courts. He was formally refused bail at a hearing on Tuesday, and the matter has been adjourned until next month.

A 43-year-old woman was also present while the fifth person has not been located.

Organised crime links still under investigation

Superintendent Moore provided an update on Tuesday. (ABC News)

Although police initially reassured the community that they did not believe the incident was related to organise crime, they later revealed they were investigating whether the men present had criminal links.

When asked about their underworld links on Tuesday, Superintendent Naomi Moore said police had "engaged" with the young boy's family before.

"A number of individuals that were inside the unit at the time are well known to NSW Police and their association with organised crime is being considered by investigators."

She also said some of those present at the home were "not co-operating with investigators", and revealed police had not yet recovered the firearm.

A resident at the unit block said police could be seen searching a nearby park and creek after the shooting.

The investigation is continuing.

Premier Chris Minns on Tuesday described the incident as an "incredibly distressing situation".

World.title: Far-right UK activist arrested after 'slashing migrant boat' at sea
World.content:
A British far-right activist known for leading protests against migrants crossing the English Channel in small boats has been arrested for allegedly slashing a dinghy at sea.

Daniel Thomas, 37, appeared to be involved in an incident showcased in a video posted to social media where he used a knife to pierce the inflatable vessel.

Mr Thomas filmed himself appearing to allegedly use a bladed weapon to pierce the inflatable exterior of a vessel being used by migrants to cross the English Channel. (YouTube: Danny Tommo)

The boat was empty of migrants, but at least one rescue service member was aboard at the time, while Mr Thomas yelled "you're in English territory" towards their direction.

"You're not using these boats, no more migrants in our country," Mr Thomas allegedly said in the video.

"This is England, this is not France … No more of this, we've taken too many."

More than 41,000 migrants crossed the English Channel between France and Britain last year. (AP: Jean-Francois Badias)

After piercing the vessel's inflatable exterior, Mr Thomas then appeared to tell the rescue workers to "get off the boat" while his own vessel began to move away.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said on Thursday, local time, that a 37-year-old man has been arrested the previous evening on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life and endangering the safety of a vessel.

The constabulary said he remained in custody on Thursday. British police do not identify suspects by name until they are charged.

The issue of migration has become a heated political topic in the UK, where protests appear to have steadily increased. (AP: Jonathan Brady/PA)

Mr Thomas, who goes by the nickname Danny Tommo, is a longtime associate of far-right activist Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, also known as Tommy Robinson.

Robinson has sparked political controversy in Australia in recent months after he interviewed One Nation leader Pauline Hanson, who blamed the end of the White Australia policy for migration issues.

A month earlier, in an interview with former Today Show host turned podcaster Karl Stefanovic, Robinson claimed Australians were losing their culture, that traditional values were under attack, and that the mainstream media was lying to its audience.

Loading...

Patriot Platform, a group Mr Thomas founded, is behind recent protests in which masked, black-clad men tried to stop migrants reaching the United Kingdom.

Earlier this month, masked demonstrators blocked the port of Dover, in south-east England, and tried to stop migrants from being taken ashore in Portsmouth on the country's south coast.

Inside Britain's battle for the grievance vote A football tragedy when he was a teenager made Britain's new PM "fall out of love" with politics. This is what it took to rebuild his trust and the lessons for Australia.

Successive UK governments have struggled to stop people — more than 41,000 last year — making the dangerous journey across one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.

The issue has been depicted as a crisis by politicians including Nigel Farage of the hard-right party Reform UK, and has been used as a rallying point by anti-immigration activists.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham's centre-left government says stepped-up law enforcement cooperation between Britain and France has helped reduce the number of people making the crossing so far this year by more than 40 per cent compared with 2025.

ABC/AP

World.title: Police investigate fatal Frankston fire
World.content:
Police are investigating a fire at a home in Melbourne's south-east that claimed the life of a woman on Thursday afternoon.

Firefighters were called to a blaze at Stanley Street in Frankston just before 5pm.

Crews arrived to find a lower level of a two-storey unit on fire, bringing it under control about half an hour later.

A yet-to-be-identified woman was found dead inside the home.

No one else was inside the property at the time.

Police say the circumstances of the fire are yet to be determined, with a crime scene now in place and an arson chemist to attend the scene.

The investigation remains ongoing.

Anyone who witnessed the incident, with CCTV/dashcam vision or information is urged to contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or submit a report online.

World.title: Former suburban Melbourne mayor jailed for sexually assaulting teenager
World.content:
A former Melbourne mayor is spending his first night in custody as part of a three-month jail sentence for sexually assaulting a teenage boy.

Warning: This story contains details that may be distressing for some readers

A suppression order was lifted on Thursday afternoon, allowing media to name Cameron Nation as the ex-Moonee Valley councillor at the centre of the case.

Nation served for 11 years as a councillor, before quitting in 2024 after an IBAC investigation found he traded cocaine for influence in planning matters.

He pleaded guilty in the Melbourne Magistrates' Court to sexually assaulting a 17-year-old boy who was under his supervision in 2019.

In jailing Nation, Magistrate Michelle Mykytowycz said his crimes were too serious for a non-custodial sentence, even though prosecutors had said it was an option open to her.

Nation assaulted 'vulnerable' teen after supplying drugs, court hears

The court heard Nation had invited the teenager, who was drunk, over to his home in December 2019.

The boy arrived around 3:30am and Nation supplied him with "nangs", also known as nitrous oxide.

Nation then pulled down the boy's pants and performed a sex act on the "vulnerable" and "spaced-out" teen, the magistrate said.

"The complainant said he felt helpless and overwhelmed," she said.

"He was not enjoying what was happening and he didn't know what to do as he had no control."

Along with jail time, Magistrate Mykytowycz also sentenced Nation to complete an 18-month community corrections order, forcing him to attend drug, mental health and sex offenders' programs.

Nation's lawyer Sam Norton said he would appeal the sentence and would lodge an application for bail next week.

Nation was charged by police in October 2025. Days later, he tried to kill himself and was hospitalised, the court heard.

A magistrate then put a suppression order in place to protect his mental health, banning reporting of Nation's name in connections with his case.

Lawyer's bid to keep Nation's identity secret fails

On Thursday, Nation's defence lawyer failed in a bid to extend the suppression order for two years, after arguing media stories posed an unacceptable mental health risk to his client.
